links.title: Family First: How Loved Ones Support Addiction Recovery in New Jersey
links.body:
## Introduction to Addiction Recovery and Family Dynamics

Addiction recovery is rarely a solitary journey. While individuals must ultimately take responsibility for their healing, the presence of supportive loved ones often makes a significant difference. In New Jersey, where communities are actively addressing substance use disorders, families play a central role in helping individuals rebuild their lives.

Recovery is not simply about abstaining from substances—it involves emotional healing, rebuilding trust, and creating a sustainable lifestyle. Families who understand this broader perspective are better equipped to provide meaningful support.

## The Role of Family in the Recovery Process

### Emotional Support and Stability

Emotional stability is one of the most critical factors in recovery. Individuals battling addiction often experience guilt, shame, and anxiety. A compassionate family environment can help counter these feelings and create a safe space for healing.

Support does not mean ignoring harmful behavior; rather, it involves empathy paired with healthy boundaries. Loved ones who actively listen and validate emotions contribute to a stronger recovery foundation.

### Accountability and Encouragement

Families also serve as a source of accountability. Encouraging consistent attendance at therapy sessions, support groups, or treatment programs can help individuals stay on track.

At the same time, celebrating small milestones—such as a week or month of sobriety—reinforces progress. Positive reinforcement can be a powerful motivator, especially during the early stages of recovery.

## Understanding Addiction as a Family Disease

Addiction is often described as a “family disease” because its effects ripple outward. Relationships may become strained, trust may erode, and communication can break down.

Recognizing this shared impact is essential. When families acknowledge their own need for healing, they are more likely to engage in supportive behaviors rather than enabling or codependent patterns. Family therapy programs in New Jersey frequently emphasize this collective approach.

## Early Intervention and Awareness

Early intervention can significantly improve recovery outcomes. Families who recognize warning signs—such as behavioral changes, withdrawal, or secrecy—can take proactive steps to address concerns.

In this context, misinformation can be harmful. For example, discussions around detox methods often lead people to questionable solutions. Articles like “Are Quick-Fix Detox Drinks Really Effective For Cleansing Your System?” highlight the importance of evidence-based approaches rather than relying on unproven remedies.

Education empowers families to make informed decisions and guide their loved ones toward professional care instead of temporary fixes.

## Common Misconceptions About Substance Use and Recovery

Misconceptions about addiction can create barriers to recovery. Some believe that willpower alone is sufficient, while others underestimate the complexity of substance dependence.

Another common misunderstanding involves exposure myths. Questions such as “Can Smelling Weed Get You High?” reflect broader confusion about how substances affect the body. Addressing these misconceptions helps families provide accurate information and reduce unnecessary fear or stigma.

By staying informed, families can replace myths with facts, fostering a more supportive and realistic recovery environment.

## Building Healthy Communication Within Families

Effective communication is the backbone of any supportive relationship. In the context of addiction recovery, it becomes even more critical.

Families should aim for open, non-judgmental conversations. Using “I” statements instead of accusations can reduce defensiveness and encourage honesty. For example, saying “I’m concerned about your health” is more constructive than “You’re ruining everything.”

Consistency is equally important. Regular check-ins and honest dialogue help maintain trust and prevent misunderstandings.

## Professional Support Systems in New Jersey

New Jersey offers a wide range of professional resources, including outpatient programs, inpatient rehabilitation centers, and family counseling services. These systems are designed to complement family support rather than replace it.

Family involvement in professional treatment often leads to better outcomes. Programs that include family therapy sessions allow loved ones to learn coping strategies, understand triggers, and rebuild relationships.

Research consistently shows that integrated care—combining medical treatment with family support—improves long-term recovery success. According to national health authorities ([Link](https://nida.nih.gov/publications/drugs-brains-behavior-science-addiction/treatment-recovery)), comprehensive treatment plans that involve family participation are among the most effective approaches to managing substance use disorders.

## Long-Term Recovery and Family Involvement

Recovery does not end after treatment. It is a lifelong process that requires ongoing effort and support.

Families can help maintain progress by encouraging healthy routines, such as regular exercise, balanced nutrition, and participation in support groups. They can also remain vigilant for signs of relapse, addressing concerns early without judgment.

Importantly, self-care for family members should not be overlooked. Supporting someone in recovery can be emotionally demanding, and maintaining personal well-being ensures that support remains sustainable.

## Conclusion: Strengthening Recovery Through Family Unity

Addiction recovery is a complex and deeply personal journey, but it is rarely successful in isolation. Families in New Jersey play a vital role in shaping recovery outcomes through emotional support, education, and active involvement.

By understanding addiction, addressing misconceptions, and fostering open communication, loved ones can create an environment where recovery is not only possible but sustainable. Ultimately, a united family approach transforms recovery from an individual struggle into a shared path toward healing and growth.

---

## English 🇬🇧

One of the places that impressed me the most during my trip to France was Château de Malmaison, the residence of Napoleon Bonaparte and Joséphine.  

There is something very different about this place compared to the typical tourist destinations. The atmosphere feels quieter, more reflective, almost frozen in time. Walking through those gardens and old paths made me think about how many decisions, conversations, and moments of history happened there centuries ago.  

As someone with a background in Chemical Engineering, I always end up observing places from two perspectives at the same time: the emotional side and the analytical side.  

On one hand, Malmaison feels elegant and peaceful. But on the other, it also reminds me how much science, engineering, logistics, and technology shaped Europe during Napoleon’s era. Many advances in chemistry, military engineering, metallurgy, medicine, and industrial processes accelerated during those years because nations were competing to survive and dominate.  

Even the architecture and garden design reveal a deep understanding of materials, geometry, drainage systems, and long-term planning. Sometimes people think science only exists inside laboratories, but traveling constantly reminds me that engineering is present in almost everything humans build.  

I also liked how natural the place feels. Huge trees, old bridges, statues hidden between the vegetation, and long silent roads create an atmosphere that almost feels cinematic.  

Sharing moments like this with my son makes the experience even more meaningful. History stops feeling distant when you can actually walk through the places where it happened.  

France has a very special way of preserving its past while still feeling alive in the present. And honestly, places like this are part of why I enjoy traveling so much.  

## Español 🇪🇸

Uno de los lugares que más me impresionó durante mi viaje a Francia fue el Château de Malmaison, la residencia de Napoleón Bonaparte y Josefina.  

Hay algo muy diferente en este lugar comparado con los destinos turísticos típicos. El ambiente se siente más tranquilo, más reflexivo, casi congelado en el tiempo. Caminar por esos jardines y caminos antiguos me hizo pensar en cuántas decisiones, conversaciones y momentos históricos ocurrieron ahí hace siglos.  

Como alguien con formación en Ingeniería Química, siempre termino observando los lugares desde dos perspectivas al mismo tiempo: la emocional y la analítica.  

Por un lado, Malmaison transmite elegancia y calma. Pero por otro, también me recuerda cuánto influyeron la ciencia, la ingeniería, la logística y la tecnología en la Europa de la época napoleónica. Muchos avances en química, ingeniería militar, metalurgia, medicina y procesos industriales crecieron rápidamente durante esos años porque las naciones competían por sobrevivir y dominar.  

Incluso la arquitectura y el diseño de los jardines reflejan un entendimiento profundo de materiales, geometría, sistemas de drenaje y planeación a largo plazo. A veces la gente piensa que la ciencia solo existe dentro de los laboratorios, pero viajar constantemente me recuerda que la ingeniería está presente en casi todo lo que construye el ser humano.  

También me gustó mucho lo natural que se siente el lugar. Árboles enormes, puentes antiguos, esculturas escondidas entre la vegetación y caminos silenciosos crean una atmósfera casi cinematográfica.  

Compartir momentos así con mi hijo hace que la experiencia sea todavía más especial. La historia deja de sentirse lejana cuando realmente puedes caminar por los lugares donde ocurrió.  

Francia tiene una manera muy especial de conservar su pasado mientras sigue sintiéndose viva en el presente. Y sinceramente, lugares así son parte de la razón por la que disfruto tanto viajar.

links.body: Od doby, kdy jsem slyšel rozdíl mezi velkou tercií a zmenšenou kviartou ve středotónovém ladění, se se mnou táhne téma zmenšených intervalů jako nosného harmonického materiálu. Dnešní den jsem začal schůzkou s Jirkou Pokorným nad harmonickým materiálem z elektroniky a dvěma klavíry impro... Vyšla nám hezká nahrávka, pracovali jsme asi dvě hodiny a to i na jeho pentatonických modech, které nakonec nesdílím, protože nejsou hotové... Pak jsme hráli Skreblink a šachy s Mirkem Schee, sdílím zde výsledek: https://youtu.be/DEbeRG71ZaQ Vytvoř básničku z následujících slov ze skreblinku: Svižna - běžkyně. Čanel - kanál. Úč - učitel. Zol - puchýř. Obát - postarat se. Husk - pejskař. Vrýh - nápis v kameni. Devím - zapomněl jsem. Sudícá - pomlouvá. Gle - lepivě. Doxo - piškvorky pro tři. Něm - zmlkni. Výněm - slova odstraněná z textu. Pozď - zpomal. Pozďar - ten, kdo se zpožďuje. Sůš - poušť. Účáf - čas na učení. Svižnan - vlak rychlík. Svižnaní - Ádéháďáci. Bilá - pravidelně bitá. Kvéti - vegani. Píň - stonek. Goan - chodec. Goane - chodče. Bop - plod ovocného stromu. Duť - vyprázdni se. Neť - surfuj po internetu. Kanic - kastrované prase. Pój - spojka. Cirh - pacient s cirhózou. Hřgle - zle. Mehy - chlupaté polštářky. Těké - reflexivní. Dyn - odumřelé rostliny. Et - ještě. At - taky. Us - usnutí.

V šachách se Mirek vzdal s věží míň.

Večer jsem dojel do Lán, kde jsme s rodiči strávili Dvořákovo Requiem. Zaujala mě práce se zmenšenou tercií a vybral jsem několik skladeb, kde se uplatňují zmenšené kroky.

Zmenšená septima v Segerově fuze \

[Fugue in F minor, /CH IX/](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IKiyVC8VzPs&list=RDIKiyVC8VzPs&start_radio=1)

Zmenšená kvinta v Bachově preludiu a fuze a moll

[Bach Prelude and Fugue No.20 Well Tempered Clavier, Book 2 with Harmonic Pedal](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1cfUVC6F0Q)

Zmenšená kvarta ve fuze cis moll:

https://youtu.be/zdD\_QygwRuY?si=HNmIs0ffykFN4Y2C

A konečně zmenšená tercie v díle Antonína Dvořáka: Requiem:

https://youtu.be/dG5Vh-ASPQc?si=mOw669IvUzc2LDPI

A konečně večer procházka s Aninou a pivku Na Růžku....

Pěkný den!

links.title: Silent Progress Is Still Progress
links.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVn84ffe6BMNybsLjw8pTvTfSF6iNbUFPVxc2sz7HMDHT/1000687249.png 

One of the most dangerous feelings in any journey is believing that nothing is happening.

You keep trying.

You keep showing up.

You keep learning.

But from the outside, it looks the same.

No applause.

No sudden success.

No dramatic transformation.

Just ordinary days repeating themselves.

And because there is no visible reward, many people start doubting their own path.

They think they are stuck.

They think they are behind.

They think everyone else is moving faster.

But what many people fail to understand is this:

Not all progress is loud.

Some of the most important growth happens in silence.

Discipline grows in silence.

Confidence grows in silence.

Skill grows in silence.

Knowledge grows in silence.

Character grows in silence.

The world often celebrates visible success, but visible success is usually built on invisible effort.

People notice the harvest.

They rarely notice the seasons of planting.

They notice the result.

They rarely notice the lonely hours of preparation.

They notice the breakthrough.

They rarely notice the years of patience behind it.

This is why many people quit too soon.

They judge their journey only by what others can see.

But real progress is not always measured by likes, money, praise, or attention.

Sometimes progress means:

You handle pressure better than before.

You recover faster from setbacks.

You know more than last month.

You are more disciplined than last year.

You kept going when the old version of you would have stopped.

That matters.

A lot.

Never underestimate the value of quiet improvement.

The habits you build today may become the strength people admire tomorrow.

The lessons you learn now may become opportunities later.

The patience you practice today may save you from quitting too early.

So if life feels slow right now, remember this:

Silence does not mean failure.

Invisible does not mean worthless.

Slow does not mean finished.

Keep going.

Keep learning.

Keep building.

Because silent progress is still progress.

And one day, what is invisible now may become impossible to ignore.

links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXRdLangtAnxpuVrz17oVNnkH7N5tUVEVVXBxVzXqHLru/1777662502196.jpg)

Good evening, blog friends, how are you? Here I am again. Today is Labor Day in Italy, and aside from some controversy about the Italian situation (if you'd like to read about it, you'll find a post on my blog), at least it's a holiday, and I've been feeling pretty good. I hadn't woken up very well because anxiety and depression seem to get a bit worse with the change of seasons, but in the end, this afternoon I felt a little better. The weather was nice, and I took a sunny walk around the city, which always boosts your mood. I also took the opportunity to stroll around the park for a bit. Going outside sometimes seems like a real chore, but when I'm outside, I feel good, and walking helps me untangle my thoughts. I'm also happy to finally be able to wear some lighter, more colorful clothes, like one of my favorite multi-colored T-shirts.

> Buenas noches, amigos del blog, ¿cómo están? Aquí estoy de nuevo. Hoy es el Día del Trabajo en Italia, y aparte de cierta controversia sobre la situación italiana (si quieren leer sobre ello, encontrarán una entrada en mi blog), al menos es un día festivo, y me he sentido bastante bien. No me había despertado muy bien porque la ansiedad y la depresión parecen empeorar un poco con el cambio de estación, pero al final, esta tarde me sentí un poco mejor. El tiempo era agradable, y di un paseo soleado por la ciudad, lo cual siempre levanta el ánimo. También aproveché para pasear un rato por el parque. Salir a la calle a veces parece una verdadera tarea, pero cuando estoy afuera, me siento bien, y caminar me ayuda a despejar la mente. También estoy feliz de poder usar por fin ropa más ligera y colorida, como una de mis camisetas multicolores favoritas.

A walk in the countryside always helps a lot. I also hope to feel better soon, although the chaos of moving, the stress, and my unemployment aren't helping at all. But maybe the longer days and getting out more could help. Anyway, I came back a little tired in the evening, but of course I made sure to have a good meal, a nice pasta with tomato sauce and tons of grated cheese (okay, I'm not really one for dieting, and it shows, hahaha). Now I'm relaxing a bit with a hilarious Korean series about Boys Love, which luckily they've translated into my language. I wanted to watch something light-hearted because I'm feeling heavy today, and cuddling my big cat—even cuddling my cats is something that has the power to relax me, especially before bed—see you tomorrow, blog friends.

> Un paseo por el campo siempre ayuda mucho. También espero sentirme mejor pronto, aunque el caos de la mudanza, el estrés y mi desempleo no ayudan en absoluto. Pero tal vez los días más largos y salir más podrían ayudar. En fin, volví un poco cansada por la noche, pero por supuesto me aseguré de comer bien, una rica pasta con salsa de tomate y un montón de queso rallado (vale, no soy muy de dietas, y se nota, jajaja). Ahora me estoy relajando un poco con una divertidísima serie coreana sobre Boys Love, que por suerte han traducido a mi idioma. Quería ver algo ligero porque hoy me siento pesada, y abrazar a mi gato grande —incluso abrazar a mis gatos es algo que tiene el poder de relajarme, especialmente antes de dormir— nos vemos mañana, amigos del blog.

links.title: La Medicina debe enfocarse mucho en las Emociones de los Pacientes
links.body: Psico neuroendocrinología es la especialidad que hoy en día muchos médicos deben buscar conocer, entender y aplicar. Está especialidad se basa en como las emociones activan una respuesta neurológica y detrás de eso una activación hormonal. El estrés mal gestionado mantiene activa dos hormonas en el cuerpo que es el Cortisol y la adrenalina, aunque son importantes en el cuerpo para la supervivencia, si se sostienen por mucho tiempo comienzan a dispararse los desequilibrios de los sistemas de órganos, aparecen dolores musculares, procesos degenerativas, células cancerígenas etc. Al entender esto el especialista se enfocaría primero en las emociones de un paciente para prevenir que su estado de salud se vea deteriorado. De este tema hay mucho de que hablar pero hasta acá dejo este threads. Gracias por leer, puede investigar más sobre esta maravilla de especialidad de la salud\n\nPosted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@magnaconsciencia/la-medicina-debe-enfocarse-mucho-en-las-emociones-de-los-pacientes-gbp)

links.title: I Known I Have Grown!!!
links.body:
There is one thing that so far, I’ve come to dislike with passion. As in, it’s been happening so often that it really irks me. However, the majority of the people who do this thing are older people, so punching them in the face might not be the best way to go about it. And as a result, I simply smile and nod at them, hoping that the conversation will be over as soon as possible. But then the irony of this is that when people around the same age as I am say these same things, I don’t really have an issue with it. Maybe because they don’t really dwell on it the same way that older people do, they simply make the observation and move on to the next thing. That way, I don’t really have to think about it or how angry it makes me. So yeah. And what is this habit I’m talking about? When people comment on how much I’ve grown. Many times, seeing elderly people I knew as a kid, I try to avoid them because the conversation is usually around the same thing. “You’ve added”, “You’re now a big boy”, “See this small boy of yesterday”, “See how your voice is thick”, “And you’re a fine man ooo”… on and on it goes. And for some reason, I find these things condescending. Like, we’ve not seen each other in 10+ years, what were you expecting? That I’d still be the same lanky teenager? It gets even worse when they try to guess where I currently am in life. Either to know my school, NYSC status, or even the job I’m doing. Note, though, I said guess, not ask. Instead of asking, “What are you doing now?” They’ll say, “you should be in 200 level now, abi?” And when I remember that the last time I saw these guys, I told them I had gotten admitted into the Higher Institution, it gets kinda frustrating. And if you talk for an hour, you’ll spend 30-45 minutes of it talking about your changes and all, and if they knew other members of your family, they’d ask about them. And then, they’d go down memory lane about how you used to be a stubborn child, running around the streets playing football. Yeah… As I said, with people closer to my age, it’s different. Because they keep it brief, “Bro, you don fresh ooo!” And that’s it. Or, “You’ve added ooo,” and it ends there. The entire conversation won’t be centered on how much I’ve changed. But on more important things. Thankfully, though, not all the older people do this. There are those whom I meet, and they’re genuinely interested in the stages of my growth, and we have deep conversations. They want too know ho school life treated me and ho I’m adapting to the labor market. How much shege the economy is showing me and the plans I have to better my life. Then, they share some advice as well. This will always be better than talking about how much I’ve changed, how I seem more mature now, and how I’m not a small boy anymore. I don’t know if I’m the only one who has been experiencing this, maybe it’s just the kind of people I have in my life. Well, at a point, it gets frustrating. This thing happened this evening as well, and I decided to come and rant here. Maybe there might be people who enjoy such conversations, but not me. And I’m slowly getting to my wits’ end. ![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHA37mQtCuynkak9C9VoqEia8jgQG2PbwFzNsktXz6Hfoe4KSQsNnmd2u5Ymq52vnQFR4CHwS2v8AuqSugp7iQ5NJr9YdH7dWYndNDhdfMi9xZHQPBjU.png](5) ***
Thank you for reading. Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments below, I would love to know what you’re thinking. Till we meet in the next post.

Coming back to COD Mobile after two months feels like stepping into your old street after a long journey. At first everywhere just looks somehow, my fingers no even dey remember the controls again. links.title: Underage Teenage Rapists Have It Way Too Easy
links.body: ![Kaazoom is the author of this picture/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2021/02/22/12/29/male-6040022_1280.jpg) ## 1.  A Tragic Rape And Murder Of A Little Girl A couple of days ago, I stumbled across a story about a 15-year-old boy named Adrian Jerry Gonzalez who raped and murdered an 8-year-old girl. She was his neighbor. This tragedy occurred in Santa Cruz, California. Below is a video that provides the entire story about it. An Underage Boy Raped And Murdered An 8-Year-Old Girl A Little Over A Decade Ago https://youtu.be/gDSQxjuDX04?si=Dh1A8cKmB1JO90iZ This boy only got four years behind bars for his crimes against this innocent little child. Have you ever noticed that in the American culture, it seems that the criminal justice system and the courts go easy on these punks no matter how heinous their sex crimes are and no matter how young their victims are? What is so outrageous is that I can't even accuse Adrian Jerry Gonzalez of being a pedophile, because the Fifth Edition of the *Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders* (\

) specifies that a pedophile can be no younger than 16 years of age.  This is not the first time that I have ever come across stories about underage teenage boys receiving a light sentence for violent sex crimes or not receiving a sentence at all or even as so much being arrested.

On the other hand, the law shows no mercy for an adult man who may be only 19 or 20 years old who gets caught having consensual sexual relations with a 15-year-old girl who suffered no harm from the intercourse.  Even worse, I'm always hearing and reading about stories about college sophomores facing lengthy prison sentences for being caught in online sex-sting operations in which they attempted to hook up with a high-school girl that didn't even exist.

The reason that punks like Adrian Jerry Gonzalez are always getting away with the kinds of heinous sex crimes that they do out in California is because the police are wasting too much of their time and resources pursuing frivolous and malicious statutory-rape cases  It's not only happening in California but in other parts of the United States as well.

Fortunately, Mr. Gonzalez was denied release once he served his four years behind bars, and, yes, he may remain on the sex-offender registry for the rest of his life.  However, you know that the court system would have gone much harsher on him if he had been a young adult male who had gotten involved in a non-violent sexual relationship with a middle-school or high-school girl than they did on Mr. Gonzalez.

Also, if Mr. Gonzalez attempts to get off the sex-offender registry, it will probably be easier for him to do so inasmuch as he was convicted of his crimes in a juvenile court.  He's going to have it much easier than an adult man would have it for a non-violent sexual offense that would be legal in most European nations.

Our society, for the most part, appears to have an attitude that teenage boys younger than 18 years old can do no wrong whenever any crime they commit involves sexual violence.  At the same time, all the self-righteous do-gooders in our criminal justice system are dead set on segregating pubescent and adolescent girls from college men any way they see fit no matter how benign such age-gap relationships may turn out to be.

The rape and murder of the above-described 8-year-old girl, Madyson Jordan Middleton (\

), took place near the Tannery Arts Center in Santa Cruz, California. If any of you are unfamiliar with it, below is a video that gives you a tour of it. A Tour Of The Tannery Arts Center In Santa Cruz, California https://youtu.be/oPhC8hvA7-A?si=C5Q_QDlK1nIzgfiU You may have noticed in the video above that there was a memorial for Maddie. The video is from a year ago, and this arts center is apparently still going strong. ## 2.  Misappropriated Police Resources Cash Jordan reports that there have been a whole host of criminal incidents out in California in which groups of people have robbed both rich and middle-class people in their own homes in even some of the most affluent neighborhoods of Los Angeles County. Below is his video. Cash Jordan Reports All The Crime And Chaos That Have Surfaced In California https://youtu.be/LUnVA63M37c?si=pm8BQIhiwZu2iJQx I realize that California, especially Southern California, has had a longstanding problem with both property crimes and violent crimes. One year when I was still living in Los Angeles, California, there were over 200 murders in one month. If anyone reading my article were living in Los Angeles during the riots there in 1992 or was watching the news about it, you may remember how people were going into grocery stores and other businesses to loot the items there. Well, it appears that what is happening now in Los Angeles County and in other parts of California is much worse than what went on back in 1992 during the L.A. riots. Does it have anything to do with Governor Gavin Newsome's policies there? I'm not going to pin all the blame on him. The core of this problem is much more elaborate than anyone cares to realize. You may or may not have seen an episode of *Dr. Phil* in which Dr. Phil McGraw held interviews with a guest panel in relation to whether or not online sex-sting operations are a form of entrapment. On that same television show, a Lieutenant Brandon Purcell from the Fresno Sheriff's Office started flapping his jaws about how these online sex-sting operations are saving the children of our nation. Then he spoke as though there was no difference between an 8-year-old child and a 14-year-old minor. Lieutenant Purcell? If you are reading this article, I can assure you that there is a world of a difference between an 8-year-old child and a 14-year-old minor. Otherwise, you would never hear about 14-year-old boys brutally raping and murdering 8-year-old girls. Moreover, no 8-year-old boy would ever rape and murder an 8-year-old girl. What really got me angry about Lieutenant Purcell is that here his state jurisidiction has serious crimes happening all around, and he and other police officers like him are too busy conducting these online sex-sting operations to do anything about those same crimes in which people are losing valuable property to them. He'd much rather be on easy street with his police duties, and proactive online sex stings are exactly that. Taxpayers have the right to complain about how police officers are spending their time and resources. If California got rid of all their online sex-sting operations and police officers went after real criminals, then perhaps California would not have the problem that Mr. Jordan described in his video above. Plain and simple. Also, Americans need to stop whining about collegiate men chatting online with make-believe 13- or 14-year-old girls, when there is an ample number of underage boys that are sexually victimizing girls this young and getting away with it. Probably the reason that girls that young are seeking relationships with older partners is because they don't trust boys their own age. You only have to look at the situation of the late Aubreigh Wyatt in which a 12- or 13-year-old boy raped her when she was 12 years old, and the police did nothing about it except for conduct an investigation that led to nothing positive. This young girl committed suicide, because the authorities and her school administrators allowed this punk to ruin her life. So, some of you are concerned that 13- and 14-year-old girls are becoming sexually active with older partners? What makes you believe that these same girls are going to be so much better off with boys their own age, when fact has it that our nation has become the deadbeat teenage dad capital of the world? Our society desperately needs a reality check. ![Megashock is the author of this image/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2019/11/27/16/47/skate-4657350_1280.jpg) ## 3.  Final Thoughts It is good that the Trump administration has cut back on Federal Funding to the Internet Crimes Against Children (\

) Task Force, but our elected officials have a long way to go before they are able to clean up all our sex laws. Unfortunately, way too many people in charge of our societal institutions are living in a make-believe world of age-appropriate perfection and wholesome purity, and they are trying to coerce others into doing so as well. If more people speak up and speak against the current American sex laws and statutory-rape laws, perhaps our elected officials will feel pressured to do the right thing and revamp our laws. The silent majority cannot remain in the shadows forever. The current sex laws and statutory-rape laws here in the United States are ruining our country. Police officers are misusing our tax dollars to go on missions and crusades to segregate adult men from teenage girls. These online sex-sting operations are teenage pregnancy-prevention campaigns at best, and they're overwhelming our criminal court dockets and penal facilities as a result of convictions for frivolous and malicious witch hunts. A journalist named Michael Tracey has even warned the public about these dangerous moral panics that are overpowering our legal institutions here in the United States. His video is below. Journalist Michael Tracey Denounces The Pedophile Panic As Being Harmful To Our Culture https://youtu.be/uwEIM7IffoA?si=WAPMlQSJuenStgXN The elephant in the room here is that way too many people, including police officers, are unable to get the definition of pedophilia right. I wouldn't doubt that Lieutenant Brandon Purcell of the Fresno Sheriff's Office watches videos like the one below. Teenage Girls Model A Casual Summer Denim Collection To Market Clothing To Middle-School And High-School Girls https://youtu.be/LNlwjEj9wvs?si=G9CYhJUsHJZAPT-t These idiots with guns and badges who view themselves to be morally perfect are usually the worst offenders of their own so-called values and principles. One day we're going to be watching the news and hear about Leiutenant Purcell getting caught with his pants down in a hotel room with a pubescent or adolescent coed, and then he won't be talking so loudly and arrogantly on these television interview shows like *Dr. Phil*. It's only a matter of time. **This article is copyright-protected.**

links.title: The Hardest Decisions We Make as Parents
links.body:
> *When it comes to preventive measures, especially vaccines, parents have different opinions…*
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmerJtbZVxcKy6oCJ5mZyKU5ktdpByZuFZEcJr8bKH2hsE/image.png)
[source](https://pixabay.com/photos/vaccine-coronavirus-medical-hand-6165772/) *When I first heard about childhood vaccines, I wasn’t too keen on my child taking them, but I wasn’t completely against it either.* *The first-week immunization was fine. The one they call BCG and a few others didn’t come with any noticeable side effects. My baby didn’t react in any unusual way.* *But the six-week vaccine? That one was something else.* *For a good 24 hours, we had no peace of mind. The baby was fussy, weak, and just didn’t look like himself. At some point, we got really scared and had to call a nurse for advice, even though the hospital had already warned us that babies might react that way.* *In the end, we gave him paracetamol and monitored him closely. Thankfully, he was fine the next day. But honestly, that experience almost made us skeptical about taking the next one.* *Out of curiosity, I went on TikTok to learn more about vaccines. That is where I came across a story of a man who lost his twins.* *According to him, everything started after they received their 6-week vaccines. The babies reacted badly, and sadly, it led to their deaths.* *Anyone who reads a story like that would definitely think twice before vaccinating their child. And then you see people in the comment section saying they never vaccinated their kids, and they turned out fine.*
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZg9zT6SCsdeaSMWL3fLvoHX9jqwcJmo6oyiZ2fKJ1fKx/image.png)
[source](https://pixabay.com/photos/woman-doctor-vaccine-covid-19-5921371/) *In my own case, my child has received all the vaccines so far. The next one is at 9 months, and honestly, I am still not sure whether he will take it. But I am not completely against vaccines either.* *For someone who has lost a child and believes it was due to vaccines, I understand why no one could ever convince them to try again. That kind of trauma is something that stays with you*. *I believe parents should have the right to make their own decisions when it comes to something as sensitive as this. It is not something anyone takes lightly, especially after seeing how a child can react or hearing painful stories from others.* *Because the truth is, when things go wrong, the same people who enforced it won’t be the ones to carry the pain.* *Imagine losing your first child because of a decision you felt pressured to make… that is not something anyone ever recovers from*. *At the same time, I understand why vaccines are encouraged and even pushed in some cases; they are meant to protect, not harm. But situations like this remind us that every child is different, and every parent’s fear is valid.* *For some, culture and beliefs also play a role, and it is not always easy to go against what you have been raised to believe; some tribes forbid their children from taking injections.* *In the end, I don’t think this is a simple “right or wrong” conversation. It is a deeply personal one. Every parent just wants to protect their child the best way they know how*.

links.title: 🇨🇺 📗 «La Vida es un Tango» de Lorenzo Lunar (ESP-ENG)
links.body:
> 📗 Saludos, amigos de #hivecuba. Con gusto les comparto hoy una reseña través de las páginas de #ecency. Se trata de la novela policial «La Vida es un Tango» del escritor santaclareño Lorenzo Lunar. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZqrHF45hsN4AC1Qei4Mbcmo232eKsevMiASya9P6YPS4/1777649966376.jpg)
***

>


He compartido café y charlas con Lorenzo Lunar en Santa Clara. He estado en su biblioteca privada, he asistido a sus peñas, lo he visto reír y callar con la sabiduría de quien escribe con las tripas. Lorenzo es uno de los grandes de la literatura policial en Cuba, con un palmarés impresionante de premios en España y toda Hispanoamérica. Y sin embargo, cuando leo La vida es un tango, no pienso en crímenes ni pesquisas.

 Pienso en los domingos.

\

, escribe Lunar. Su narrador recuerda aquellos otros: el olor de las frituras de harina y el chocolate caliente que preparaba su viejo. Las flores de Hilda. La tía que iba fiel al cementerio donde dormía su hijo muerto por \
. Los negritos del solar con sus ropitas blancas, remendadas pero limpias, porque \

. Cundo, Tachuela y Bola de Queso amaneciendo en la esquina, borrachos de alcohol de reverbero, cantando rancheras trágicas con la guitarrita vieja de Pedrusco. La pelota detrás del cementerio. Las bandadas de pajaritos rumbo al Parque Vidal.

Esa Cuba profunda que está en estas páginas no es la de los eslóganes. Es la Cuba del barrio, del solar, de la madre que reprocha porque el protagonista no ha llamado a Luisa, del primo Jorgito cuyo retrato cuelga en la sala, de la tía Hilda que en paz descanse. 

Una Cuba que lacera porque se reconoce en estas páginas de Lorenzo.

Paradigmático suele parecer el narrador- protagonista en el inodoro, porque ese es el único tiempo que le queda para pensar. El polvo blanco que se derrama en la letrina, juntándose con los excrementos. El tipo llamado Chago que le dice: \

. 

Lunar mezcla el policial con la crónica de una vida ordinaria, y el resultado es devastador.

Pero el corazón verdadero de la novela está en el epílogo. \

, repite el narrador. No viene la pipa de cerveza, la gente protesta, pero él es feliz. Se va a levantar a la hora que le salga de sus entrañas. Va a afeitarse sin apuro, a bañarse con agua tibia todo el tiempo que quiera. Va a buscar a su hija, la va a montar en un coche de chivos viejos en el Parque Vidal, le va a comprar un globo y caramelos, van a repugnarse comiendo helados en Coppelia.

Porque tiene derecho a un domingo.

Esa frase —\

— es quizás la más política de toda la novela, aunque no mencione ni un solo partido ni una sola ley. Porque hay días que se vuelven trincheras. Hay horas que son actos de resistencia. Elegir la lentitud cuando todo exige prisa, elegir el calor del agua cuando sobra la indiferencia, elegir el paseo en coche de chivos viejos sobre el asfalto roto de Santa Clara: eso no es evasión, eso es afirmación. Es decir: existo, quiero, permanezco. Lorenzo Lunar ha escrito una novela policial que no trata de policías. No hay herejes que atrapan villanos, ni crímenes que se resuelven con guantes de látex y lámparas de escritorio. Lo que hay, en cambio, es algo más difícil de atrapar: hay una memoria que se niega a ser borrada, una dignidad que aprende a caminar entre grietas, y esa pequeña rebeldísima —la más frágil y la más poderosa— de ser feliz cuando todo amenaza a no serlo. El crimen, quizás, no es un asesinato: es el robo cotidiano de la alegría. Y el detective, entonces, es cualquiera que decide recuperar su domingo. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWyRQQfxcNbpQNaME7KcgVSvoPLa6FahtaRsUbSNrKumH/1777649985193.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/un-edificio-alto-con-un-reloj-en-la-parte-superior-igwC6S_Br4w)
***

> Gracias a él por esta y todas sus novelas, y gracias a ti, estimado hiver, por llegar hasta esta reseña y seguir hasta el final. Porque leer también es una forma de hacer pausa. Porque detenerse en las palabras de otro es, al fin y al cabo, concederse ese domingo que nadie nos regala. Y ahora, sí, la pregunta para mis seguidores, para los que quedaron hasta el último renglón, para los que también saben lo que duele y lo que cuesta: ¿Cuál fue la última vez que te regalaste un domingo fuera del calendario? Ese día que no estaba marcado en rojo, que nadie te dio, pero que tomaste para ti —con agua tibia, con un helado, con una tarde sin prisa— como un acto de ternura y de guerra a la vez? Cuéntamelo. Porque quizás, al leerte, yo también aprenda nuevas formas de ser feliz. **© Marabuzal, 2026. Todos los derechos reservados.** ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVDUKVA6YugQdRrhGACmnps8ddBkV8W6UwGEo9DwaNQxF/1768408479017.jpg)

>

📗 Greetings, friends of #hivecuba. I'm happy to share a review with you today through the pages of #ecency.

It's about the crime novel \

by the Santa Clara-born writer Lorenzo Lunar. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZqrHF45hsN4AC1Qei4Mbcmo232eKsevMiASya9P6YPS4/1777649966376.jpg)
***

>

I've shared coffee and conversations with Lorenzo Lunar in Santa Clara. I've been to his private library, attended his literary gatherings, and seen him laugh and fall silent with the wisdom of someone who writes from the heart.  Lorenzo is one of the greats of Cuban crime fiction, with an impressive list of awards in Spain and throughout Latin America. And yet, when I read *Life Is a Tango*, I don't think about crimes or investigations.

I think about Sundays.

\

Lunar writes. His narrator remembers those other Sundays: the smell of fried dough and the hot chocolate his father used to make. Hilda's flowers. The aunt who faithfully went to the cemetery where her son slept, dead from \
The little Black children in the tenement with their white clothes, patched but clean, because \

Cundo, Tachuela, and Bola de Queso at dawn on the corner, drunk on cheap alcohol, singing tragic rancheras with Pedrusco's old guitar. The ball behind the cemetery. The flocks of little birds heading towards Vidal Park.

 The deep Cuba found in these pages isn't the Cuba of slogans. It's the Cuba of the neighborhood, the tenement, the mother who scolds the protagonist for not calling Luisa, the cousin Jorgito whose portrait hangs in the living room, Aunt Hilda, may she rest in peace.

A Cuba that wounds because it recognizes itself in these pages by Lorenzo.

The narrator-protagonist often seems paradigmatic on the toilet, because that's the only time he has left to think. The white powder spilling into the latrine, mixing with the excrement. The guy named Chago who tells him: \

Lunar blends crime fiction with the chronicle of an ordinary life, and the result is devastating.

But the true heart of the novel lies in the epilogue. \

the narrator repeats. The beer truck doesn't arrive, people complain, but he's happy. He's going to get up whenever he feels like it.  He's going to shave without rushing, to bathe in lukewarm water for as long as he likes. He's going to pick up his daughter, put her in an old goat cart in Vidal Park, buy her a balloon and candy, and they're going to devour ice cream at Coppelia.

Because he has a right to a Sunday.

That phrase—\

—is perhaps the most political in the entire novel, even though it doesn't mention a single party or a single law. Because there are days that become trenches. There are hours that are acts of resistance. Choosing slowness when everything demands haste, choosing the warmth of the water when indifference abounds, choosing the ride in an old goat cart on the broken asphalt of Santa Clara: that's not escapism, that's affirmation. That is to say: I exist, I want, I remain. Lorenzo Lunar has written a detective novel that isn't about police officers. There are no heretics who catch villains, nor crimes solved with latex gloves and desk lamps. What we find, however, is something harder to grasp: a memory that refuses to be erased, a dignity that learns to walk among cracks, and that tiny, almost rebellious act—the most fragile and the most powerful—of being happy when everything threatens to deny it. The crime, perhaps, isn't murder: it's the daily theft of joy. And the detective, then, is anyone who decides to reclaim their Sunday. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWyRQQfxcNbpQNaME7KcgVSvoPLa6FahtaRsUbSNrKumH/1777649985193.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/un-edificio-alto-con-un-reloj-en-la-parte-superior-igwC6S_Br4w)
***

> Thanks to him for this and all his novels, and thanks to you, dear hiver, for reaching this review and continuing to the end. Because reading is also a way to pause. Because pausing to reflect on the words of another is, ultimately, granting yourself that Sunday that no one else gives us. And now, yes, the question for my followers, for those who stayed until the very last line, for those who also know what it hurts and what it costs: When was the last time you gave yourself a Sunday outside of the calendar? That day that wasn't marked in red, that no one gave you, but that you took for yourself—with warm water, with ice cream, with a leisurely afternoon—as an act of tenderness and of defiance at the same time? Tell me about it. Because perhaps, by reading your words, I too will learn new ways to be happy. (Google Translation) **© Marabuzal, 2026. All rights reserved.** ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWjfrW9s6z2APoqFnoXCffUb7S5Nu2p75P5VZgoJ5o7ej/1777314040592.jpg)

Hello my lovely friend's, How was our day. I welcome you all to my blog @amara24. It's another week to display our shadows as lovers of #shadowhunters and am glad to share with you all my shadow hunt for the new month.

For a week now, the NEPA has refused to supply power to us and the weather has been so hot because the sun its af if its close to the earth. So have this fan i always charge once i see the sunrise and it's been very useful to be during the night.

Immediately i saw the sun, i took the solar fan outside to recharge, as I dropped it, i noticed the shadow of fan, as a lover of shadow who is always ready and alert to hunt for shadows. I happily went inside the room to get my phone and there i capture it.

links.title: MY HANDCRAFT THAT MAKES LIFE EASY
links.body:
Hello, everyone, you are welcome to my blog today.

When I came across this weekly prompt my heart leaped for joy because this is an experience I have been waiting to share because I surprise myself most times when I do this and guess what it generated a lot of income for me in school and it saved me of personal expenses in school and I’m very grateful for it and always want to help people around me with it , discovering my talent is the best thing that has happened to me till date , lets dive into the fully story.


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmejAKGqhA4SjtExdEbH3TgL1KJJeZCmngBaaBiRXNqeXe/173803.jpg 


My mom was one of those women who don’t want to spend their money in hair salons she would sit me down and use a black thread to do the legendary syngas hair style or tie tie to my hair that was the only hairstyle she knew, not minding if I loved it or not. But she always did it so well and they always turned out neat and perfect and sometimes she would make little gowns for me with her sewing machine and the funny part is that she never learned any of this and that was just her God giving talent I’m always amazed when I watch her sew.

Growing up into a beautiful young lady and I got into secondary I realized I could weave my hair myself ,wow I was amazed because I didn’t learn this anywhere as time went by and I got into the university and that was another world of its own and as a student you are not supposed to depend solely on your parents so during my time in the hostel my room mates noticed one thing about I never patronize any hair dresser in school because I just go to the internet and pick a hairstyle I want to make and I do it perfectly on myself they were all shocked and marveled at how beautiful it turned out.




So they started booking me to make their hair for me and they paid for my services they will always ask where did you learn and I will say no I didn’t I just know my way around and my creativity was top notch ,this skill or talent has helped me in so many ways and to think I never learnt it for a day i became well known for my skills till I graduated .


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTK5TS1uFyZfQbrxBMds2Jx8gZaWJmef968iiw1nMjeQx/173804.jpg 




And till date I can count how many times I have gone to a saloon to sit down to get my hair done, I do that by myself and to my ladies out there who can understand the cost of making hair now so I must say I’m very lucky to have such a skill and talent I never learnt.

Thank you for stopping by my blog today.



Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@betheloji12/my-handcraft-that-makes-life-easy-fec)

links.title: The US banned Anthropic... but Mythos is the exception.
links.body:
/>

The U.S. Department of Defense has classified Anthropic as a supply chain risk, preventing the developer's AI from being used in government applications. However, Mythos, a model focused on cybersecurity, is being closely monitored by the government and may be an exception.

I think the issue of Mythos, which is being addressed across the government, not just the War Department, is a separate national security moment where we need to ensure our networks are hardened, because this model has specific capabilities to find cyber vulnerabilities and fix them.

The assessment was made this Friday (1) by the agency's technology director, Emil Michael, during CNBC's Squawk Box program. According to him, Claude Mythos is a special case, as it has strategic relevance for US national security.

The statement comes after a standoff between the Pentagon and Anthropic, which gained momentum earlier this year. The government wanted unrestricted use of Claude in military applications, while the developer did not authorize its use in tasks considered dangerous, such as citizen surveillance and autonomous weapons. Olhar Digital broke down this dispute here.

**Despite restrictions, the US is using Mythos**

Despite the formal restrictions, the situation is more complex in practice.

According to CNBC, there are reports of the company's models being used in operations related to the war against Iran, as well as indications that Mythos is being employed by the National Security Agency (NSA). This context raises questions about how the government can use the technology without contradicting its own guidelines.

**News item retrieved from the Samir News website.**

links.title: (ENG/ESP) 🐱🎨💻 Let's Make a Collage - Round 249: Cats own the internet / Los gatos son dueños de la red 🐱🎨💻
links.body:
#
ENGLISH CONTENT

Hello to all members of this community and collage lovers! Today I woke up wanting to make collages, so after sitting down to create a physical collage, I decided to get to work on my entry for the [contest](https://peakd.com/hive-174695/@lmac/lets-make-a-collage-a-contest-for-all-creatives-on-hive-round-249-55-hive-in-the-prize-pool), before I forgot about it, because the days go by so fast and I get busy haha. Luckily, the electricity held up during the collage-making process, although I had to jump through hoops to write this post, as the platform's image upload function was failing me 😩 Anyway, this was the result I got:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPtbgZHBAsTmqBnWWMDCpyPMbNFDJoPe8w99ygd4DcGHS/1777660167991.png)

When I saw @seckorama's image, I thought of someone being protective of others. My idea was to draw a little girl being protected by the figure, perhaps from the rain or something else. However, I changed my mind and decided that the creatures being protected would be cats. It's no secret that for years, cats weren't among the most popular pets, and in many cases, when someone adopted a cat, it wasn't with the intention of giving it care and affection, but rather to use it as a pest control agent. All that changed with the rise of the internet, where cat lovers began to show that tender and charming side that many were unaware of, ultimately capturing the hearts of people who never imagined they would want to care for a feline.
|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcTZFXSGnfNZRwSv5zafFWpNqRdmpnwZ6F9BEQudi6BRS/1777659597875.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQman9YEjQUnAL5ovLKT944BPbbsfsdQXW9LrV9V8XGBDfK/1777659658967.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTqh7fKVpSkXTAT6TxhKLpvEhbGrmPKH34ywGVBVKYVjk/1777659597918.jpg)| |-|-|-|
However, even though cats go viral simply for lying on the floor, there are also those who wish to harm them. How much evil must reside in a heart to want to hurt a defenseless animal? I try to avoid certain news stories, but when I come across cruel acts against these little animals, my heart aches. I want to believe that all these cases of abuse will receive due justice, because these atrocious acts should not go unpunished.
|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYbH4T5bvbJQgPnR91SJ1NS5irVfscKnsvSdJ7Uqx9KjB/1777659597955.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV8nndFMXntMcWuQuqFogskRHiKTxovJeQ6Hn84HMVxdq/1777659597985.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd6zYbQUMp15frksqXM5WaZJHaNJcidCac8cQJnorvFV8/1777659598019.jpg)| |-|-|-|
To create the collage, I used the program *Photoshop* and at the end, I added some effects with the apps *Line Camera* and *Vaporgram*, in order to obtain an image that gave the illusion of being part of the **Dreamcore** aesthetic, because sometimes, I feel that real life is like oscillating between the most fascinating dreams and the most improbable nightmares.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmekQFtyL2jtwRcACPK3wqWb8S891wJQN6bCsikVRp8bAM/1777659659033.jpg)

#
CONTENIDO EN ESPAÑOL

¡Hola a todos los integrantes de esta comunidad y amantes de los collages! Hoy me desperté con ganas de hacer collages, así que luego de sentarme a realizar un collage físico, decidí ponerme a trabajar en mi participación para el [concurso](https://peakd.com/hive-174695/@lmac/lets-make-a-collage-a-contest-for-all-creatives-on-hive-round-249-55-hive-in-the-prize-pool), antes de que se me olvidase, porque los días pasan rápido y me ocupo jaja Por suerte, la energía eléctrica se mantuvo en el proceso de elaboración del collage, aunque tuve que hacer maromas para escribir la publicación, pues la carga de imágenes de la plataforma, me estaba fallando 😩 En fin, este fue el resultado que obtuve:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPtbgZHBAsTmqBnWWMDCpyPMbNFDJoPe8w99ygd4DcGHS/1777660167991.png)

Cuando vi la imagen de @seckorama, pensé en alguien siendo protector con otros. Mi idea era hacer una niña siendo protegida por la figura, tal vez por la lluvia o algo más. Sin embargo, cambié de parecer y decidí que fuesen gatos las criaturas a ser protegidas. Para nadie es un secreto que por años, los gatos no eran parte de las mascotas favoritas y en muchos casos, cuando alguien adoptaba un gato, no lo hacía con las intenciones de darle cuidados y mimos, sino más bien para utilizarlos como un eliminador de plagas. Todo eso cambió con el auge del internet, en dónde los amantes de los gatos comenzaron a mostrar ese lado tierno y encantador que muchos desconocían, acabando por acaparar los corazones de las personas que nunca se imaginaron que tendrían deseos de cuidar a un felino.
|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcTZFXSGnfNZRwSv5zafFWpNqRdmpnwZ6F9BEQudi6BRS/1777659597875.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQman9YEjQUnAL5ovLKT944BPbbsfsdQXW9LrV9V8XGBDfK/1777659658967.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTqh7fKVpSkXTAT6TxhKLpvEhbGrmPKH34ywGVBVKYVjk/1777659597918.jpg)| |-|-|-|
Sin embargo, aunque los gatos sean virales hasta simplemente por echarse en el suelo, también han aparecido quienes desean hacerles daño ¿Cuánta maldad debe haber en un corazón para querer hacerle daño a un animal indefenso? Trato de no enterarme de ciertas noticias, pero, cuando me encuentro con actos malvados hacia estos animalitos, mi corazón se apretuja. Quiero creer que todos esos casos de maltratos recibirán su debida justicia, pues esos actos atroces no deben quedar impunes.
|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYbH4T5bvbJQgPnR91SJ1NS5irVfscKnsvSdJ7Uqx9KjB/1777659597955.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV8nndFMXntMcWuQuqFogskRHiKTxovJeQ6Hn84HMVxdq/1777659597985.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd6zYbQUMp15frksqXM5WaZJHaNJcidCac8cQJnorvFV8/1777659598019.jpg)| |-|-|-|
Para la realización del collage, utilicé el programa *Photoshop* y al finalizarlo, le agregué algunos efectos con las app *Line Camera* y *Vaporgram*, con el fin de obtener una imagen que diera la ilusión de formar parte de la estética **Dreamcore**, pues a veces, siento que la vida real es como oscilar entre los sueños más fascinantes y las más inverosímiles de las pesadillas.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmekQFtyL2jtwRcACPK3wqWb8S891wJQN6bCsikVRp8bAM/1777659659033.jpg)

links.title: Why Publishing a Research Paper is Important for a University Student
links.body:
I believe that there is a time in the life of most university students when someone talks of publishing a research paper and the first thought is confusion or fear. I experienced the same. It was as though it were a part of an entirely new world. A place of older professors, lab coats and complex scholarly terms that was not to be accessed by regular students like myself. I used to hold on to that belief a long time and no one around me bothered to rectify that. And that, I believe, is quite an indignity since the reality is quite different than I supposed.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdcSpGui8mXwwrD3FtYRs77A2C2f6cQaPvXUhdC1v2nDy/andre-william-NDGIibZRa_0-unsplash.jpg 
[Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/white-printer-papers-NDGIibZRa_0)

I would like to tell you what I have learned about this to understand better. A research paper is not a long complex task. It is an opportunity that a student has to get serious about something he has studied, develop his original thought about it and present it before the rest of the world in a manner that is believable. By the time that paper is published it will mean that people outside your university, people who have no personal interest in taking the trouble to be nice to you, have read your work and found that it has some real merit. I believe that sort of validation is extremely uncommon and extremely strong to a young individual who is still trying to discover himself/herself in terms of academics.


Practically speaking the relevance of releasing a research paper in university years is an issue I am very much concerned with. The environment students are leaving in the present world is highly competitive. All people are degree holders. All are good students and have a resume of activities. Yet not all have made the leap of making something new to their discipline even when they are a student. It is a small difference on paper but it is felt. It is observed by universities that provide postgraduate programs. It is noticed by employers who desire individuals with the ability to think independently. I think it is one of the few things a student can accomplish in his or her university life that will indeed distinguish them among the crowd in any significant way.

I believe, though, the benefits that occur within an individual are no less important than the benefits that are posted on a resume. Composing and publishing a research paper can teach a student how to pose the correct questions concerning a problem. It educates them on the process of finding information that is real and not mere convenient. It teaches them to develop an argument carefully and make it sound in such a way that others can follow and believe it. I had been through this procedure and I will be frank to say that it has altered something in my mode of thinking. Not only during academic work but in normal situations as well. It helped me be more cautious on my opinion making and more serious on finding the right grounds before I believe in something.

It also has the confidence attached to it that I did not anticipate. Prior to the process I never felt that my thoughts and observations mattered enough to be shared outside my classroom. Having read it I no longer felt like that.

In all fairness I believe that each and every university student is entitled to learn about this opportunity much earlier than the vast majority of them do. I am sure that the right information at the right time can transform a lot of things.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@mimiuse/why-publishing-a-research-paper-is-important-for-a-university-student-5ga)

links.title: Vaccines vs Beliefs: Where Should the Line Be Drawn?
links.body:
We all know how important vaccines are to human survival in this world plagued by different forms of sickness and diseases. We've seen through the years how vaccines have saved lives through generations; take for instance prior to the discovery and administration of polio vaccines, we've seen lots of people get plagued with the illness and become unable to walk, but since their discovery, the plague of polio has become a thing of the past, and many now live and walk thanks to the preventive vaccines they took at one point in their lives. But then, despite how wondrous most vaccines are, should people be allowed to decline taking them due to their beliefs or concern about their safety? https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTRPWfWmKr1QLt7QhHzKwAL4r7iCF7ZFtwMr85jCE3eiB/1000857092.png This is actually a very complicated topic to delve into because I'm put in the middle of a medical necessity and religious beliefs, and we all know these are two top-tier topics that draw altercation when one is contradicted. But then, if I'm to state my personal take on this, I'll say everyone should do what works for them, knowing fully well that they'll bear the consequences of their actions. But even at that, we need to be wise and understand that for God to have given humans knowledge to have a breakthrough in that aspect, then it'll be unwise for us to refuse medical procedures that'll ensure our safety. Take for instance, a few days ago, I came across a post where a man talks about his mother-in-law encounter at a hostel, where a woman was told she'll need to undergo CS to give birth, but the woman's mother refuses, saying their pastor has assured them she'll give birth by herself. Not long after that, the pastor even came to pray for her. But the man who posted the story said his own mother-in-law approached the mother of the other pregnant woman, offering to cover the expenses of the CS, but was abused for such suggestions. At the end of the day, the pregnant woman died during labor, and her mother, who refused to let her undergo CS, ended up bringing a tricycle to carry her dead body. Although the above story isn't related to vaccines, we all can see how medicine and belief sometimes clash and the harsh implications that could lead to. Vaccines are good and important for our wellbeing, safety, and prevention from terrible sickness or disease; we've vaccines that, when gotten, safeguard one from diseases such as polio, hepatitis, and the like. Now imagine not taking those vaccines and ending up being plagued with any of those diseases; you'll end up having yourself to blame. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmakPdR47AYoVpSuK8yoMijfusE24MTgaw1ugdU8FAJtJN/1000857093.png On the other hand, I understand some people's reservations about vaccines; take for instance many don't want to take covid vaccines because most of those who took them were said to die or end up being plagued with the virus. In light of that, one can stay safe by not talking about it. I fit; I didn't take the COVID vaccine, and to date I'm fine. When it comes to how parents act on behalf of their kids by refusing to have them take vaccines, we can't entirely blame them. What I think we should do is educate them on the importance and dangers of not getting them for our kids. I remember a case of how twins of some new parents in Lagos mysteriously died after taking a vaccine; to date no one knows what actually caused it—maybe it was an overdose, wrong medication, or whatever. And these are reasons why people create barriers to safeguard themselves and their children from being victims of the same fate. So in a nutshell, we should create more awareness and sensitization, and medication practitioners should be more careful when doing the jobs. *** All photos are taken and edited on canva. ***
Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@vickoly/vaccines-vs-beliefs-where-should-the-line-be-drawn-jdu)

links.title: The Renaissance the the USA Didn't Want You to Know About - 07-27-2017 - 10X Speed
links.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1777663579329-76013a3f40c08bf9.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/cf2ff5a8)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/cf2ff5a8)


---

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

---

links.title: Consultorio Day, Here We Are 💚✨ / Día de Consultorio, Aquí Estamos 💚✨
links.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQHdzTeqe7KPxXFQyxWX9akQY4Uc3oZaWnLBPPwBeeVbk/IMG_7285.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRNity1BMQrLZy1zwQqp9WgBjf7kzGjq7uixVts4U57pj/IMG_7284.jpg 

Today is a consultorio day, so here we are, ready to give our best. I always feel a special kind of energy when I arrive — it’s like stepping into a space where I can truly make a difference. Every patient that walks in brings a unique story, and I love being able to listen, guide, and support them on their journey toward better health.

Preparing my space, organizing everything, and welcoming each person with a good attitude is part of what I enjoy the most. It’s not just about giving recommendations, it’s about creating trust and helping people feel comfortable enough to believe in their own progress.

Being here reminds me why I chose this path. It fills me with purpose and gratitude. So yes, today is consultorio day, and I’m here, present, motivated, and happy to do what I love. 💚✨

Hoy es día de ir al consultorio, así que aquí estamos, listas para dar lo mejor. Siempre siento una energía especial cuando llego — es como entrar a un espacio donde realmente puedo hacer una diferencia. Cada paciente que entra trae una historia única, y me encanta poder escuchar, orientar y acompañar en su camino hacia una mejor salud.

Preparar mi espacio, organizar todo y recibir a cada persona con buena actitud es algo que disfruto mucho. No se trata solo de dar recomendaciones, sino de generar confianza y hacer que las personas se sientan cómodas para creer en su propio proceso.

Estar aquí me recuerda por qué elegí este camino. Me llena de propósito y gratitud. Así que sí, hoy es día de consultorio y aquí estoy, presente, motivada y feliz de hacer lo que amo. 💚✨

links.title: Rostros del primer día de mayo / Faces of the First Day of May [ES/EN]
links.body:
>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmet8NVgKojjufPV2yv2ZYQEPdpLxaHPQV6PZoCQxG5AEw/portada.jpg)

Comienza mayo, el quinto mes del año. Mayo: mes de los trabajadores, mes de las flores, mes de las madres. Mayo caribeño que llega  promocionando el sol del eterno verano que distingue a esta parte del planeta. Mayo que viene a refrescar las tardes con sus aguaceros que la tierra agradece. 

>May begins, the fifth month of the year. May: month of workers, month of flowers, month of mothers. Caribbean May arrives promoting the sun of the eternal summer that distinguishes this part of the planet. May comes to refresh the afternoons with its downpours, which the earth appreciates.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQdbeCXG4RZcgPdf3Wv5WWU5hQJREVFFBfGoWiTLiotnQ/19.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaLV8TuQC9k119LwrCmr8Djp6u7MmNJdsV9BUYrzsoEYS/2.jpg)

El primer día de Mayo tiene un rostro peculiar.  Rostro que compone el caleidoscopio de un pueblo sencillo y trabajador. Y a pesar de que a este mayo le bastan razones para el descontento, la cámara atrapó muchas sonrisas dispuestas a cerrar el paso a la tristeza. El simple motivo de vivir el primer día de mayo fue suficiente. 

>The first day of May has a peculiar face. A face that composes the kaleidoscope of a simple and hardworking people. And although this May has ample reason for discontent, the camera captured many smiles determined not to give way to sadness. The simple reason of experiencing the first day of May was enough.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2p2S2kqWPMNmuxYVxa4RdRfqPYS42eiWKYooWvQzLNy/1.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNwm5HogzfMs6B8JaFQt3fmAaTgvYRnG6yqcqYpSkhNfB/16.jpg)

Mayo empieza con la fiesta de una marcha por la Patria. Cada uno de los que estábamos allí sentimos algo más que “…el amor ridículo a la tierra…”  y  “…a la yerba que pisan nuestras plantas…”. Otros, aunque no recibieran los rayos del sol de este primer día de mayo en las calles y plazas de la isla, también son necesarios para sostener la Patria. 

>May begins with the celebration of a march for the Homeland. Each of us who were there felt something more than “…the ridiculous love for the land…” and “…for the grass under our feet…”. Others, although they did not receive the sun's rays on this first day of May in the streets and squares of the island, are also necessary to sustain the Homeland. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZUifgRYixdMHJnfX88YuvJ3MUV7Lw6eCvEedG8KSVj6h/3.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ2Wmm5df54iBrh4HuWDHuJ5B7Sx4N5VdwsoXoZ8s9UN4/4.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb9Rwiv3bmP67yVpcW2zQrWMqSmbJF4gJRotcYqe2K1L2/5.jpg)

En estos tiempos de prepotencia sin límites. Cuando se ha puesto de moda el irrespeto a las reglas internacionales de convivencia y a la paz, sentí que mi deber, como dijo el poeta, era “alzar la bandera, sumarme a la plaza” 
>In these times of boundless arrogance, when disrespect for international rules of coexistence and peace has become fashionable, I felt that my duty, as the poet said, was to \

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU7eNh3D47FWGYHC796orc3ab1KaeUw4E8yd5w3nUgSYa/6.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZg4tHiFX7Hk8C2ePJ38sv2wTVkvPQCTAkVkzHn6UfULD/7.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcRnRm2KNKD8cezPypepvErjnUdb2LZEpgc1vcbszGRL8/8.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQvTAYVGZpoYrxypUZfrLRBxtpYsgXmMiSSN18WZ7HZw2/9.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZh8zWVhcRmg6k4gvPKXhMgojSStMPtCHnP8kT55j8YTo/10.jpg) Los rostros inaugurales de mayo visten el honor de mentes y manos trabajadoras. En ellos está la fuerza capaz de superar la crisis que nos golpea. Ellos tienen el poder de la transformación necesaria, que nace desde las raíces, para hacer florecer y fructificar el árbol que nos cobija a todos. >The faces of this May's inaugural celebrations wear the honor of hardworking minds and hands. In them lies the strength capable of overcoming the crisis that strikes us. They possess the power of the necessary transformation, born from the roots, to make the tree that shelters us all flourish and bear fruit. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWgExNU4bpCLNVzrhuGGG56ir5gHK6uWs6ZCBpEJiQpVX/12.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYCFpgaGUK8XvnQh6aNynVFzwNFbsvdqKCsWVUPADiyzF/13.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ7L7i4PxaQeQgzhQxa6Mb82g3AmVPJmtTcF36oLAKmiB/14.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYczS4svVQZExzbjKoF8eAUjg7meSgd6dRc3MEqNKXd7C/15.jpg) Este primer día de mayo, puede marcar la arrancada para llegar a la meta. Los comienzos tienen esa magia. Nos permiten trazarnos caminos por recorrer. Muchas veces no nos damos cuenta de que solo es necesario dar el primer paso. >This first day of May can mark the starting point for reaching the finish line. Beginnings have that magic. They allow us to chart paths to follow. Many times we don't realize that it's only necessary to take the first step. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNaFDybswH5zp6on1PmUvWTvg58kxkFpH5YmuNZPn4Jdp/17.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQARrm2TUgK2XU72LUckiEJPxnutpo4YUhEVtdhuGNfJc/18.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSNZZv74fGienEWZY2KiQt7akLYKEss6Q8ACVWXcU4AAv/20.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYvA4EGaHZiV9t4GPfM3fcYtdqEjBQGNvrfANAiDKhFXk/21.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTa8Qkr7vayTUL7y1DnxyR2L1fNwMiajRx97DmzsvtiSV/22.jpg) Puede que parezca imposible, pero lo peor es no intentarlo. En ocasiones nuestro pesimismo es el mayor de los frenos. Más aun cuando se convierte en un sentimiento colectivo. Por suerte, siempre aparecen osados decididos a romper la inercia. >It may seem impossible, but the worst thing is not to try. Sometimes our pessimism is the greatest obstacle, even more so when it becomes a collective feeling. Fortunately, there are always bold individuals determined to break the inertia. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS4y7Tff1Lvs9jxY5pvZWH1LNr3trTweRKj1K9uhLPCX7/11.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma9XpaD3EMJD7DX6esRpT1XBA6EzKS5VuWbiaBBmqkFH2/23.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeJBjAg6A8Zev7QW7h3H3fVo6AWDa7GYvYSRqTxwapJh7/24.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmchwC8jE8xqr6BiDQwPrfE8NxZiGZqLWVNokk1c9qwRiv/25.jpg) Aquí están los rostros de este comienzo de mayo. Hay otros, que pueden reflejar las tristezas y desesperanzas que hoy nos acompañan. Pero estos fueron los que yo vi esta mañana y quise compartirlos con ustedes. Muchos encontraran, en ellos, su reflejo. Estoy seguro que toda esa gente también cargaba con sus crisis internas, pero hoy tocaba engalanarle el semblante al primer día de mayo. >Here are the faces of this beginning of May. There are others that may reflect the sadness and despair that accompany us today. But these were the ones I saw this morning, and I wanted to share them with you. Many will find their own reflection in them. I'm sure all those people were also carrying their own inner turmoil, but today was a day to brighten up the first day of May. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRWWmwqdq7EVaemnRC81xvG8iw4VW2pviqTJ6dkDhKLzh/26.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdsgALww8Ae7bRnWDeeY7pnva2MMKB7sYEFYBRWYTvjH2/27.jpg)
![separador hive.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leopard0/Eo6JzjYaJjrNwqT4hweuNknHA1pE33cEL6jyw7PJpUq8mv3iv4CDjeyt19M9ern59gZ.png) Contenido original de ✏️ Original content by @leopard0 Escrito original en Español ✒️ Translated with [DeepL.com](https://www.deepl.com/es/translator) (free version) Imágenes propias 📸 Own pictures
