body.body: >\n\nPresentamos la trayectoria de **Iris Gavidia**, la voz caraqueña que bajo el nombre de **\
** se convirtió en un referente de la música llanera y el sentimiento romántico en Venezuela y México.
>\n\nWe present the trajectory of **Iris Gavidia**, the Caracas voice who, under the name **\

**, became a reference for llanera music and romantic sentiment in Venezuela and Mexico. -----
[English version below!](#contenido-english)
----- ![iris.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/musicavenezuela/AKwN1cBgoe1GbHoPuuokp9TvXreFXYYKJrpTce8Ham1xL6K86i7oBZibmeowfey.png) # Iris Gavidia: La Potra que conquistó el llano y la ciudad
>\n\nLa trayectoria de **Iris Gavidia**, conocida universalmente como **\

**, es un ejemplo de constancia y evolución dentro de la música venezolana. Aunque nació en Caracas, su identidad artística se fundió con el estado Aragua al establecer su vida en La Victoria. Su camino en el arte comenzó a la temprana edad de 14 años con una determinación profesional clara. Inicialmente, su registro vocal y sus gustos personales la inclinaban hacia el bolero y géneros románticos, pero el destino la condujo hacia la música tradicional. En este campo, fue cofundadora del **Grupo Vera**, una experiencia fundamental donde popularizó temas como **\

**, aunque su estancia en esta agrupación fue solo una parte de su largo proceso de formación.\n\n**Iris Gavidia** debió recorrer un camino de trece años de actividad profesional, fogueándose en diversos escenarios y formatos, antes de consolidar su primer proyecto discográfico como solista. Este debut ocurrió de la mano de uno de los productores y compositores más influyentes del país: el maestro **Hugo Blanco**. Bajo su tutela, la cantante incursionó en la música llanera con un éxito inmediato y arrollador. De esta unión creativa, y bajo la pluma de **Blanco**, nació el tema **\

**, una canción que no solo dominó las carteleras radiales, sino que le otorgó el apodo artístico con el que el público la bautizó para siempre.\n\nSu versatilidad técnica le permitió trascender el arpa llanera, siendo invitada de honor por la **Rondalla Venezolana** para participar en una de sus prestigiosas producciones. En este proyecto, **Iris Gavidia** grabó el tema **\

**, demostrando su maestría para navegar entre la reciedumbre del folklore y la suavidad de las guitarras románticas. Esta capacidad de adaptación la llevó también a cruzar fronteras, logrando un impacto notable en México. En tierras aztecas, fue distinguida con el premio **La Nota Musical de Oro**, un reconocimiento otorgado por medios de comunicación y empresarios artísticos mexicanos en honor a su trayectoria y a su labor de difusión de la cultura venezolana en el exterior. En su etapa más reciente, tras culminar varios ciclos exitosos con **Hugo Blanco**, **Iris Gavidia** ha tomado las riendas de su carrera de manera independiente. En esta fase, ha lanzado producciones en un estilo llanero con matices más líricos, fusionando la fuerza de su apodo con la sensibilidad de sus inicios en el bolero. Su carrera es el testimonio de una artista que supo esperar el momento justo para brillar, manteniéndose hoy como una de las figuras femeninas más respetadas de la escena musical nacional, demostrando que el talento y la autenticidad son las mejores credenciales para permanecer en el gusto del público por décadas. -----
Who Conquered the Plains and the City\n\nThe career of **Iris Gavidia**, universally known as **\

**, is an example of perseverance and evolution within Venezuelan music. Although born in Caracas, her artistic identity merged with Aragua state when she established her life in La Victoria. Her journey in art began at the early age of 14 with clear professional determination. Initially, her vocal range and personal tastes inclined toward bolero and romantic genres, but destiny led her toward traditional music. In this field, she was a co-founder of **Grupo Vera**, a fundamental experience where she popularized songs like **\

**, although her stay in this group was only one part of her long training process.\n\n**Iris Gavidia** had to travel a path of thirteen years of professional activity, performing in various settings and formats, before consolidating her first recording project as a soloist. This debut occurred at the hand of one of the country's most influential producers and composers: master **Hugo Blanco**. Under his tutelage, the singer ventured into llanera music with immediate and overwhelming success. From this creative union, and under the pen of **Blanco**, the song **\

** was born, a track that not only dominated the radio charts but also gave her the artistic nickname by which the public baptized her forever.\n\nHer technical versatility allowed her to transcend the llanera harp, being a guest of honor of the **Rondalla Venezolana** to participate in one of their prestigious productions. In this project, **Iris Gavidia** recorded the song **\

**, demonstrating her mastery in navigating between the strength of folklore and the softness of romantic guitars. This adaptability also led her to cross borders, achieving a notable impact in Mexico. In Aztec lands, she was honored with the **La Nota Musical de Oro** award, a recognition granted by Mexican media and artistic entrepreneurs in honor of her career and her work in spreading Venezuelan culture abroad. In her most recent stage, after completing several successful cycles with **Hugo Blanco**, **Iris Gavidia** has taken the reins of her career independently. In this phase, she has released productions in a llanera style with more lyrical nuances, merging the strength of her nickname with the sensitivity of her early days in bolero. Her career is the testimony of an artist who knew how to wait for the right moment to shine, remaining today as one of the most respected female figures on the national music scene, proving that talent and authenticity are the best credentials to remain in the public's taste for decades. #

body.title: Arrival in England: 873 CE.
body.body: > Layla returned to the Animus after reviewing a mysterious message, leading to Eivor's arrival in England in 873 CE. Upon finding the river blocked by a massive chain, Eivor volunteered to go ashore alone. Utilizing Synin for scouting and stealthy aerial paths, I began assassinating the camp's defenses to clear the way. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmabMLdYHBdbNikJNyJkZ4XkKBsNWGzwbYSiZnU2akCsjG/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWJV7gFfHYR3g8AkCgVBriQhnwWvmTNiDrR3VNV4vfWN8/screenshot_2_.png) After I was satisfied exploring around the small cabin in the woods, I decided to go back to the Animus to continue the journey. While Rebecca was mentioning that the trip from Norway to England takes about a week by longship, she noted she would just grab the data ahead to save time. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUSpbRMKAvCnmYPQDmFMLWoGBGtqvdKhQ5JZdwVoVwn7t/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVndQvZWqVL9UYNeEu8iun8pQ2PVdPVpuU2eYisXSZKuz/screenshot_4_.png) Layla was still feeling the shake inside her head from the bleeding effect, and then she asked Rebecca if she could play the message again to find some clarity. Shaun mentioned they had already transcribed the audio if Layla was looking for something specific, but she insisted on hearing the original recording one more time. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeqKves9uVuyCL1gF5WXvtrNhvHTBBRVBfPpYa6Gp15Fj/screenshot_5_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZGh85q5tvVRhng8RjMaCwQTA2xW4w1QVnzzkt3g8MrR4/screenshot_6_.png) Before getting back into the Animus, she listened closely to the recording that led them to this burial site. After hearing the special message that mentioned Eivor, the Wolf-Kissed, Layla finally felt ready to settle into the animus. The transition began, and the modern world faded away as the simulation initialized the lush, green landscapes of a new country. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXNTnxFZLMnkUsnHpXdenjqG7Vivt1LoGKkXDMPFyUMeC/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYVERsXHuxxvTEdcGVP1hwBbsL5GfrFjsYE6goN2n2VG4/screenshot_8_.png) It looked like the Raven Clan had finally reached England, and the interface confirmed it was 873 CE. The longships cut through the water of the river. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNq5QptRxdS8KEhqtgJNJ1GiYMet1acJh6GszY6ZorrSM/screenshot_9_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYYs6Ns99yKT1e4gyPjLXrBFvX2N1HrtYfv43i6Z72o6S/screenshot_10_.png) While the warriors reached England, Dag mentioned they would make this land their own soon enough. Eivor mentioned he was glad to see any land at all and would be happy to have feet on solid ground again. They had been on the boat for a few weeks, and the constant rocking of the sea had made everyone restless. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXnxiXnhubVeTK2tJooa4hH5CDEhoAcU9bE5nCdW3sXkr/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUZywcrAj2DEpcw6ngNwLQN6vVbLDwds5yu76qu976oiD/screenshot_12_.png) While the warriors on the boat were having various conversations, they suddenly saw people drowning a dead body along the banks, while they had to reach a settlement further down the river. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbDTrrZNy8KLtTHQLAYL2J4aZQ7UMCpZcaX3587e6Js2i/screenshot_13_.png) Suddenly I noticed some kids were running through the shore and then some horse riders were also riding fast toward the nearby woods. Their hurried movements somehow told me there were problems around. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRm9fFXpj44L7ABvjjYoZuGJ1hoGPjUa3kEjf8L9HXZgH/screenshot_14_.png) After rowing the boats for a moment, they found the way forward was blocked by a massive iron chain spanning the river. The obstacle was a clear sign of a local garrison's defense, and it was a tool they must remove before pressing on further inland. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSRGkUrJ7jde7YPF26mUrkE9gYPeV7gngJswnfnVx4HYY/screenshot_15_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPVMhp9YcUDgcbYuQPPDTntvw5PchwBhHrukMWEx4yzMv/screenshot_16_.png) Sigurd mentioned there must be a way to release the chain in the nearby camp, as the links were too thick for axes to break. So Eivor volunteered to go alone while the boat stayed behind in cover. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRWEdLT9owbQFiuhBEZeZCS1kXwr68QW985FcqZo2Uvmx/screenshot_17_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaCiFYTjUYMNWiBYX7tz3y1mNvHzv71GLfoECZvhRyuST/screenshot_18_.png) I climbed up this tree to get a better vantage point, and from what I could see, there was an archer on the tower nearby. I called Synin, my raven, to check out the place first and mark the locations of the other soldiers. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmThThcFPdUoM3zCVxqe3vgHqwMf3j9LSAxsngfFGSR3m2/screenshot_19_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZXzwUEiEVAgrXzFwYiLAd38DfHCRbbxYpzojFW81a4Rd/screenshot_20_.png) Then I assassinated that archer from the tower and pulled down his body all the way to the ground to keep the platform clear. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWiwRhDpkHjCLEuYmr5bJEBCn8RhLGQ6XaeSBLqS7DJ4j/screenshot_21_.png) Now that I knew there were more enemy soldiers around, I started moving through aerial paths to take it slow and quiet. I didn't want to make a mess in a new land so early in our arrival. That's all for now. --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=coooldude/6dbae800)

body.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 1 2026
body.body:
Some mornings just pull you outside without much convincing. Started with a quiet walk while the streets were still waking up. I wasn’t in a rush, just letting the body loosen up. After a bit, I drifted into a light jog, then paused for some stretching near the park—nothing structured, just working through tight legs. The rest of it turned into this loop of walk, jog, stretch… repeat. Somewhere along the way, I realized I’d already gone further than planned, but it felt too good to stop. Ended up around 18,000 steps by the time I got back. It’s strange how the body resists at first but settles in once you give it time. Not every session needs intensity—sometimes flow does more. If you’re unsure about heading out, keep it simple. Start slow and let the rest figure itself out.
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@ghouse25/actifit-ghouse25-20260501t170341965z)_

body.body:
<center>![](https://arcange.eu/images/HiveAnalytics-EN-GC.jpg)</center>

### Welcome to the monthly analytical report about the Hive blockchain.

All the information presented in this report is based on the data collected from the blockchain until 2026-04-30 midnight UTC. This report aims to provide you with a clear view of what is happening on the Hive blockchain.

### 1. New users

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-AccountsNew-EN.png)

This chart shows the number of newly registered users on the blockchain and how many of them became active. The chart is kind of dynamic! A user can register one day and become active a few days later. Therefore, the number of active users on a specific date may change from day to day.

|||
|-|-|
|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-AccountsCreators-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Accounts-EN.png)|

These two graphs show who created new accounts during the last day and the total number of registered accounts. The red line shows how many of them have been active at least once (active meaning publishing a post, commenting or voting). They are included even if they become inactive later.

### 2. Active users

|||
|-|-|
|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Actives-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Actives30-EN.png)|

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-ActivesMonth-EN.png)

These graphs show the activity of users over time and in more detail the last 30 days. In these graphs, \

are those performing any type of transaction on the blockchain.
The last graph is a monthly summary of the active users. Be careful when interpreting the value of the last column which can be much lower if the end of the month has not yet been reached.

### 3. Apps

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-AppsSocial-EN.png)

This graph shows which applications are most used to publish posts and comments. Please note that the same user can use several different applications.

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-AppsCustom-EN.png)

This graph shows which applications generate the most activity (custom_json operations) on the blockchain.

### 4. Posts And comments

|||
|-|-|
|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Posts-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Posts30-EN.png)|

These graphs show the evolution of posts and comments for the whole blockchain lifetime and the last 30 days.

### 5. Curation

|||
|-|-|
|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Votes-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Votes30-EN.png)|

These graphs show the evolution of curation (upvotes) for the whole blockchain lifetime and the last 30 days.

### 6. Daily transactions

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-Transactions-EN.png)
||||
|-|-|-|
|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-TransactionsPerBlockMAX-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-TransactionsPerBlockAVG-EN.png)|![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-TransactionsPerBlock48-EN.png)|

These graphs show the number of transactions per day, and the highest number of transactions per block, the average number of transactions per block, and the number of transactions per block for the last 48 hours. This gives you an idea of the whole activity on the blockchain.

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-TransactionsTypeDay-EN.png)

This graph shows the distribution of the top 10 types of transactions by number of operations performed on the blockchain.

### 7. Communities and Tags

![](https://arcange.eu/hive-images/2026-04-30-CommunitiesSubscribers-EN.png)

This graph shows the communities with the most subscribers.

|||

# Learn Zig Series (#35) - Cross-Compilation and Target Triples

## Solutions to Episode 34 Exercises

**Exercise 1** - Linear search vs binary search benchmark:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{@as(f64, @floatFromInt(best_linear)) / @as(f64, @floatFromInt(best_binary))});
}
```

Linear search touches every element until it finds the target (O(n)), binary search halves the range on every step (O(log n)). With 1M sorted elements, binary search wins by roughly 3 orders of magnitude because log2(1,000,000) is about 20 comparisons vs up to 1,000,000. Binary search starts winning at surprisingly small sizes -- even around 32-64 elements it's competitive, and by 128 elements it's consistently faster. The key prerequisite is that the data must be sorted, which is why we initialized `data[i] = i * 3` in ascending order.

**Exercise 2** - SoA particle simulation with bit-packed active flag:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{countActiveSoA(soa.active)});
}
```

The SoA layout wins for `updatePositions` because the hot loop only touches x, vx, and active -- three contiguous arrays vs a struct where those fields are interleaved with y, vy. The `countActive` comparison is even more dramatic in SoA: one packed `bool` array vs scanning 20-byte structs just to read a single flag. Regarding the bit-packed variant with `ArrayBitSet` -- in practice it can be slightly faster for `countActive` (popcount over packed bits is very efficient) but slightly slower for the conditional update because extracting individual bits has more overhead than reading `[]bool`. The tradeoff depends on whether you're memory-bound (bit packing helps) or compute-bound (direct bool access helps).

**Exercise 3** - Naive vs transposed vs tiled matrix multiply:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{
            n,
            @as(f64, @floatFromInt(best_naive)) / 1e6,
            @as(f64, @floatFromInt(best_trans)) / 1e6,
            @as(f64, @floatFromInt(best_tiled)) / 1e6,
        });
    }
}
```

The naive version suffers from terrible cache behavior in the inner loop: `b[k * n + j]` strides through column elements of `b`, jumping `n * 8` bytes per iteration -- which is a cache miss on every access at larger sizes. The transposed version fixes this by making the `b` access contiguous (`bt[j * n + k]`). The tiled version keeps 32x32 blocks in L1 cache, reducing memory traffic dramatically for n=512. At size 128 all three are similar (128*128*8 = 128KB fits in L1), at 256 you see the first divergence, and at 512 the tiled version is typically 2-4x faster than naive. LLVM does vectorize the inner `j` loop in the tiled version -- you can confirm by checking for `vfmadd` or `vmulpd`/`vaddpd` instructions in the objdump output.

Alright, today we're leaving the single-machine world behind. Everything we've built so far -- the data structures, the performance-tuned code, the state machines, the memory-mapped I/O -- all of that was compiled for whatever machine you happened to be sitting at. But one of Zig's most celebrated features is that it can compile for virtually ANY target platform from ANY host platform, with zero external toolchains required. No installing cross-compilers. No docker containers with ARM sysroots. No struggling with `apt-get install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu`. Just Zig ;-)

If you've ever tried cross-compiling a C or C++ project -- say, building an ARM Linux binary on your x86 Mac -- you know the pain. You need a cross-compiler, the right libc headers, matching shared libraries, and usually quite some voodoo with pkg-config paths and sysroot directories. Zig ships all of this BUILT IN, and it's not some second-class feature -- it's a core design goal of the language.

## What target triples are: arch-os-abi

When you compile code, the compiler needs to know three things about the target machine: what **CPU architecture** it runs (x86_64, aarch64, riscv64, etc.), what **operating system** it uses (linux, macos, windows, freestanding, etc.), and what **ABI** (Application Binary Interface) it expects (gnu, musl, msvc, eabi, etc.).

Zig combines these into a target string formatted as `arch-os-abi`. Some examples:

- `x86_64-linux-gnu` -- 64-bit Intel/AMD Linux with glibc
- `x86_64-linux-musl` -- 64-bit Intel/AMD Linux with musl libc
- `aarch64-linux-gnu` -- 64-bit ARM Linux (like Raspberry Pi 4, AWS Graviton)
- `aarch64-macos-none` -- Apple Silicon macOS
- `x86_64-windows-gnu` -- 64-bit Windows with MinGW ABI
- `riscv64-linux-gnu` -- 64-bit RISC-V Linux
- `wasm32-freestanding-none` -- WebAssembly (no OS)

You can see the full list of supported targets by running:

```
zig targets | python3 -m json.tool | less
```

This dumps a JSON blob with every supported arch, OS, and ABI combination. The list is enormous -- Zig supports over 60 architectures and dozens of OS/ABI combinations. Not all combos are valid (you can't have `x86_64-macos-gnu` because macOS doesn't use glibc), but the valid combinations cover basically every platform you'd want to target.

The **ABI** part is the one most people find confusing. On Linux, you mostly care about two choices: `gnu` (glibc -- the standard C library on most distros) and `musl` (a minimal, statically-linkable alternative). Programs linked against `musl` produce fully static binaries with zero runtime dependencies -- you can literally `scp` the binary to any Linux machine and it runs. Programs linked against `gnu` typically need the matching glibc version on the target, which is why you sometimes see errors like \

when running binaries on older distros. For maximum portability on Linux, `musl` is almost always what you want for Zig programs.

On Windows the ABI is `gnu` (MinGW-style) or `msvc` (Visual Studio-style). Zig can target both but `gnu` doesn't require the MSVC runtime DLLs, so it's simpler for standalone tools.

## Cross-compiling from one OS to another

Here's the part that blows people's minds if they're coming from C/C++. Let's say you're on a Linux x86_64 machine and you want to build a binary for macOS on Apple Silicon. In C, you'd need to install a cross-compiler toolchain, get the macOS SDK headers, configure your build system to find everything, and pray. In Zig:

```
zig build-exe main.zig -target aarch64-macos-none
```

That's it. One flag. Zig produces a Mach-O binary that runs natively on Apple Silicon Macs. No SDK needed, no Xcode, no additional downloads. Zig ships with the necessary header definitions and linker support built in.

Going the other direction works too. On your Mac:

```
zig build-exe main.zig -target x86_64-linux-musl
```

You now have a static Linux binary. Copy it to any x86_64 Linux box via scp and run it. No dependencies whatsoever because musl was linked statically.

Let's write a simple program to demonstrate this in practice:

```zig
const std = @import(\
)`\n\nWhen writing cross-platform code, you often need different behavior depending on the target. Zig handles this entirely at compile time using `@import(\

, .{config});
}
```

The critical thing to understand is that `builtin.os.tag`, `builtin.cpu.arch`, and `builtin.abi` are all **comptime-known values**. When you write `if (builtin.os.tag == .windows)`, the compiler evaluates this condition at compile time. In a Linux build, the entire Windows branch is completely eliminated from the binary -- not just skipped at runtime, but never compiled at all. This means you can have platform-specific code that references headers or APIs that don't exist on other platforms, and it won't cause errors as long as it's behind the correct comptime branch.

This is a massive advantage over C's `#ifdef` preprocessor approach. In C, conditional compilation uses string-based preprocessor directives that don't participate in the type system. In Zig, it's just regular `if` and `switch` on typed comptime values, with full IDE support, type checking, and refactoring tools.

## Platform-specific code paths with `switch (builtin.os.tag)`

For more complex platform differences, a `switch` on the OS tag (or CPU arch) is cleaner than nested if-else chains:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{timer.elapsedMs()});
}
```

Because `switch (builtin.os.tag)` is evaluated at comptime, the compiler eliminates all branches that don't match the target platform. The resulting binary only contains the code for the platform it was built for. This gives you the convenience of a single source file that handles multiple platforms, with zero runtime overhead for the platform dispatch.

Note how this works naturally with Zig's error handling and type system. You don't need special macro languages or conditional compilation pragmas. It's just normal Zig code that happens to branch on comptime-known values. As we saw in [episode 15](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig) when we looked at `build.zig`, the same `builtin` values are available in build scripts too -- your build logic can add platform-specific source files, flags, or libraries based on the target.

## Testing cross-compiled binaries with QEMU

Building for a diffrent platform is great, but how do you actually TEST those binaries without the physical hardware? QEMU to the rescue. QEMU is a machine emulator that can run binaries compiled for other architectures. For our purposes, QEMU's \

is the interesting bit -- it translates foreign instruction sets on-the-fly so you can run, say, an ARM binary on your x86 Linux machine.

Install QEMU user-mode emulators:

```bash
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install qemu-user qemu-user-binfmt

# After installing, ARM and RISC-V binaries \

transparently
# because binfmt_misc registers the handlers with the kernel
```

Now build and test:

```
zig build-exe hello.zig -target aarch64-linux-musl -O ReleaseSafe
qemu-aarch64 ./hello

zig build-exe hello.zig -target riscv64-linux-musl -O ReleaseSafe
qemu-riscv64 ./hello
```

With `qemu-user-binfmt` installed, the kernel intercepts foreign binaries automatically, so you can even run them directly without the `qemu-aarch64` prefix:

```
zig build-exe hello.zig -target aarch64-linux-musl
./hello    # kernel detects it's ARM, routes through QEMU transparently
```

This makes it practical to run your test suite against cross-compiled builds. In your `build.zig` you can configure test steps that use QEMU as the test runner:

```zig
const std = @import(\

),
            .target = b.resolveTargetQuery(t),
            .optimize = optimize,
        });
        b.installArtifact(exe);
    }
}
```

Build everything with one command:

```
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe
```

After this completes, `zig-out/bin/` contains:

```
zighash-x86_64-linux
zighash-aarch64-linux
zighash-x86_64-windows.exe
zighash-aarch64-macos
```

Four platform-native binaries from one source file, one build command, one machine. No Docker, no VMs, no cross-compiler packages, no CI matrix of different OS runners. Just Zig.

The Linux builds are statically linked against musl, so they run on any Linux distro without shared library dependencies. The Windows build uses the MinGW ABI, so it runs without needing MSVC redistributables. The macOS build produces a Mach-O binary for Apple Silicon.

This is the pattern you'd use for release automation. Your CI pipeline runs `zig build` once, collects the four binaries from `zig-out/bin/`, and uploads them as release assets. If you need to support more platforms (32-bit ARM for older Raspberry Pis, RISC-V, FreeBSD, etc.), just add more entries to the `targets` array.

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- Target triples follow the `arch-os-abi` convention -- Zig supports over 60 architectures and dozens of OS/ABI combos out of the box
- Cross-compiling in Zig is a single `-target` flag, no external toolchains needed -- build Linux ARM binaries on macOS, Windows binaries on Linux, anything from anywhere
- WebAssembly is targeted as `wasm32-freestanding-none` with `export` functions and `-dynamic` linking
- Zig bundles glibc and musl as source and compiles them on-the-fly for the target, which is also why `zig cc` works as a C cross-compiler
- `@import(\

)` gives you comptime access to the target's arch, OS, and ABI -- conditional branches on these values are eliminated entirely by the compiler, zero runtime cost
- `switch (builtin.os.tag)` is the idiomatic way to write platform-specific code in Zig -- no preprocessor macros, just normal typed expressions
- QEMU user-mode emulation lets you run and test cross-compiled binaries on your dev machine -- Zig's build system integrates with it automatically
- A single `build.zig` can define targets for every platform, producing all binaries in one `zig build` invocation

## Exercises

1. Write a program that prints detaled system information: CPU architecture, OS, ABI, pointer size, endianness, page size, and (on Linux/macOS) the value of the `HOME` environment variable or (on Windows) the `USERPROFILE` variable. Cross-compile it for `x86_64-linux-musl`, `aarch64-linux-musl`, and `x86_64-windows-gnu`. If you have QEMU installed, run the ARM binary and verify it reports `aarch64` as its architecture.

2. Create a `build.zig` that builds a small library (a string utility with `contains`, `trimLeft`, `trimRight`, and `toUpper` functions) for 3 targets: native, `aarch64-linux-musl`, and `wasm32-freestanding-none`. The Wasm target should `export` all four functions. Write tests that run for the native and ARM targets (using QEMU for ARM). Verify the `.wasm` output exists after building.

3. Write a program that uses `switch (builtin.os.tag)` to implement a `listDir` function that prints directory contents. On Linux and macOS, use `std.fs.Dir.iterate()`. On Windows, also use `std.fs.Dir.iterate()` but prefix the output with the drive letter from `std.fs.cwd().realpathAlloc()`. On `freestanding`, make it a `@compileError`. Cross-compile for all three OS targets and verify that the freestanding build fails with your custom error message while the others compile successfully.

Bedankt en tot de volgende keer!

body.title: Example 5: Horizontal Distance Traveled by a Projectile
body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![Fc1kAVS7wcfNpR7N_5_Projectile_Distance.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/mes/images/Fc1kAVS7wcfNpR7N_5_Projectile_Distance/Fc1kAVS7wcfNpR7N_5_Projectile_Distance.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

In this video, I determine the vector formula for path of a projectile launched at an angle by integrating the acceleration due to gravity acting on it, and then integrating its velocity vector. When the y-component of the position vector is equal to zero (i.e. the object strikes the ground), the corresponding non-trivial time variable corresponds to the horizontal distance traveled. This distance is maximized when the launch angle is π/4 radians or 45 degrees.

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=mes/8dbed9fa) - [YouTube](https://youtu.be/usBTdTWAugs) - [Telegram](https://t.me/meslinks/34567) - [Summary](https://inleo.io/threads/view/mes/re-leothreads-ise7bvlp) -  [Notes](https://peakd.com/hive-128780/@mes/e443f9d3) - [Sections playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLai3U8-WIK0Hxo8aPU3ezG0tcLvgJnxLB) - [Vector Functions playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLai3U8-WIK0HQl7xTQBS_O8Te8PcpNm4U) - [MES Links](https://mes.fm/links)

body.title: Short Term Cash Loans: A Practical Guide for Managing Temporary Money Gaps
body.body: Money stress doesn’t usually come from big, dramatic decisions. More often, it shows up quietly—an unexpected bill, a delayed payment, a car issue that can’t wait, or a week where expenses simply arrive faster than income. For many Australians, these moments create short-term pressure rather than long-term financial trouble.\n\n

/>

  
That’s where [**short term cash loans**](https://www.loansbuddy.com.au/short-term-loan/) often enter the conversation.  
These loans are frequently talked about, sometimes criticised, and often misunderstood. Some people see them as a quick solution, others as something to avoid completely. Like most financial tools, their usefulness depends on how and why they’re used.  
This guide explains short term cash loans in Australia in a clear, realistic way—without hype, without judgement, and without complex financial language. The goal is to help you understand what they are, how they work, and when they may—or may not—be appropriate.  
**What Are Short Term Cash Loans?**  
Short term cash loans are loans designed to cover temporary financial shortfalls. They’re typically smaller in amount and meant to be repaid over a relatively short period, often ranging from a few weeks to a few months.  
The key idea is timing, not wealth.  
These loans are not intended for lifestyle upgrades, long-term investments, or major purchases. Instead, they’re meant to help people manage short gaps between income and expenses.  
**Common situations where people consider short term cash loans include:**  
• Urgent household bills  
• Car repairs needed for work  
• Medical or dental expenses  
• Emergency travel  
• Bridging a gap between pay cycles  
They exist because real life doesn’t always align neatly with payday.  
**Why Short-Term Cash Problems Are So Common**  
Even people who budget carefully can find themselves short on cash at times. Financial pressure isn’t always the result of poor money habits.  
**Some common reasons Australians experience short-term cash issues include:**  
• Rising living costs  
• Casual, contract, or self-employed income  
• Reduced work hours  
• Unexpected repairs or health costs  
• Delayed payments  
• Supporting family during emergencies  
In many of these cases, the issue isn’t a lack of income overall—it’s timing.  
**How Short Term Cash Loans Work in Australia**  
While different lenders may have different processes, [**short term cash loans in Australia**](https://www.loansbuddy.com.au/short-term-loan/) generally follow a similar structure.  
**Loan Amounts**  
These loans usually involve smaller sums, often from a few hundred dollars up to a few thousand. The amount is typically linked to income and repayment ability rather than assets.  
**Repayment Period**  
Repayment periods are short by design. Some loans are repaid within weeks, others over a few months. Repayments are often aligned with income cycles—weekly, fortnightly, or monthly.  
**Application Process**  
**Applications usually focus on:**  
• Proof of income  
• Identification  
• Basic expense information  
The process is often quicker than traditional long-term loans, reflecting the short-term nature of the borrowing.  
**Short Term Cash Loans vs Other Types of Loans**  
It’s important to understand how short term cash loans differ from other financial products.  
**Short term cash loans:**  
• Are designed for immediate, temporary needs  
• Involve smaller amounts  
• Have shorter repayment periods  
• Focus on short-term affordability  
**Long-term loans, on the other hand:**  
• Support major purchases  
• Involve larger sums  
• Stretch repayments over years  
• Require long-term financial planning  
Using a short term loan for a long-term problem often leads to stress.  
**When Short Term Cash Loans May Be Helpful**  
Short term cash loans can be useful in specific, limited situations, especially when the alternative creates more harm.  
**They may make sense if:**  
• The expense is unavoidable  
• You have stable income  
• You know exactly how and when you’ll repay  
• The loan solves a timing issue, not an income issue  
For example, someone with a steady income facing an urgent bill before payday may use a [**short term loan**](https://www.loansbuddy.com.au/short-term-loan/) to manage cash flow rather than affordability.  
**When Short Term Cash Loans Can Cause Trouble**  
Problems tend to arise when short term loans are used without a clear plan or as a recurring solution.  
**They may not be suitable if:**  
• You’re already struggling with ongoing expenses  
• Repayments would require borrowing again  
• The loan is for non-essential spending  
• There’s no clear repayment strategy  
Short term loans are not designed to fix long-term financial hardship.  
**Understanding Costs and Fees**  
In Australia, loan fees and charges are regulated, but it’s still essential to understand what you’re agreeing to.  
**Short term cash loans may include:**  
• Establishment fees  
• Ongoing account fees  
• Fixed charges or interest  
Because the loan period is short, costs can appear manageable upfront. However, borrowers should always look at the total amount repayable, not just individual fees.  
**Key questions to ask:**  
• How much will I repay in total?  
• When are repayments due?  
• What happens if I miss a payment?  
Clarity upfront prevents stress later.  
**Responsible Lending in Australia**  
Australian lending laws require lenders to follow responsible lending practices. This includes assessing whether a loan is suitable and affordable for the borrower.  
**This framework aims to:**  
• Reduce financial harm  
• Prevent unaffordable lending  
• Improve transparency  
However, even with regulations in place, the borrower’s own judgement remains important.  
**Alternatives to Short Term Cash Loans**  
Before applying for a loan, it’s often worth considering other options.  
**Depending on the situation, alternatives may include:**  
• Asking service providers for payment extensions  
• Using emergency savings  
• Seeking help from community organisations  
• Accessing financial counselling  
• Talking to employers about pay timing  
Short term cash loans are usually best viewed as one option among many, not the first or only choice.  
**Planning Repayments Before You Borrow**  
One of the most overlooked steps in borrowing is planning repayment before applying.  
**Ask yourself:**  
• Will repayments fit comfortably into my budget?  
• What expenses will I need to cut back on?  
• What happens if income changes unexpectedly?  
A loan should ease pressure, not add to it.  
**The Emotional Side of Financial Decisions**  
Financial stress affects decision-making. Urgency can push people to act quickly, sometimes without fully understanding the consequences.  
**Taking time to:**  
• Read terms carefully  
• Do simple repayment calculations  
• Consider alternatives  
can make a significant difference. Even a short pause can turn a rushed decision into a thoughtful one.  
**Using Short Term Cash Loans Responsibly**  
When used responsibly, short term cash loans can provide temporary relief. The key is intention.  
**Responsible use usually involves:**  
• Borrowing only what’s needed  
• Having a clear repayment plan  
• Avoiding repeated borrowing  
• Treating the loan as temporary support  
If borrowing becomes frequent, it may be time to reassess underlying financial challenges.  
**Building Better Financial Buffer Over Time**  
While this guide focuses on short term solutions, long-term stability matters too.  
**Small steps can help reduce future reliance on loans:**  
• Setting aside small emergency savings  
• Tracking expenses more closely  
• Adjusting budgets as costs change  
• Seeking financial advice when needed  
Financial resilience builds gradually, not instantly.  
**Final Thoughts**  
[**Short term cash loans**](https://www.loansbuddy.com.au/short-term-loan/) exist because life doesn’t always cooperate with financial plans. When money gets tight temporarily, they can offer breathing room—if used thoughtfully.  
Understanding how these loans work, recognising their limits, and planning repayments carefully allows Australians to make informed decisions without unnecessary stress.  
A short term cash loan should help you regain balance, not create a new problem. The most important part isn’t the loan itself—it’s knowing when it truly fits your situation.

body.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1777654712265-77bc92fe9a8cd962.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=valentinazoera/d4b52b89)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=valentinazoera/d4b52b89)


---

¡Hola, Amiguitos, Papitos y ZoeTubers! Tengo la dicha de presentarles uno de los poemas más largos e intensos del poeta y escritor salvadoreño, Alfredo Espino. El poema se llama: \

, que pertenece a su libro de poesía Jícaras  Tristes, Auras del Bohío. 

Acuarela Salvaje representa la inmensa belleza y autenticidad de la flora animal,  entre armonía y lucha, luz y oscuridad se enfrenta,  símbolo y superficie, así como cuando nos aferramos a la vida; entre tu dulce aliento que se pierde a través de mi suspiro... 

Es el toro. Tan negro, que causa la impresión
de una bella escultura cincelada en carbón.
Sobre el repecho yergue su indómita arrogancia,
mientras todo un boscaje le rinde su fragancia...
___

Dedico este poema a todos mis suscriptores fieles e incondicionales que tienen el buen gusto de disfrutar mis poemas y cuentos infantiles, les mando muchas energías positivas y un fuerte abrazo 🤗✨

¡Espero disfruten muchísimo! 😉

---

body.title: Interview Gone Wrong — Fiction.
body.body: Well, this interview didn't go as planned in any way, I was sure my ancestors were looking down at me from the great beyond and saying, *\

* to all of my thoughts.




It started when I woke up the morning of the interview and couldn't remember any of those things I had taken my time to read and memorize for the past one week.




 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYbV9zBLcdeFhuTEM1xyFrqpEiTSrPCeBxn7nQ4M7BqpY/1000996443.png 




I brushed through my books and decided to read it on my way down to the venue. I took my bath and mid bathing, water stopped coming. Well, I had to use my towel to clean the soap on my body and go get dressed. As you can see, it was no looking like it at all.



One of the worst shock came when I find out that the suit I had ironed just the day before was looking rough, as if I had used it to fight somebody or something. I began to think and ask myself questions, *\

* Well, what would you have me do, I put it on as it is.





As I stepped out of my room, the sitting room was unusually filled up, that's not a common thing in my house, I told them good bye and someone responded with, *\
* My mum added.\n\nI was about to go back and find out who talked first... Something like... *\

* In Funnybros voice..😂😂




All thanks to God, I was able to get a bus fast, I brought out a sheet of paper I had tore along and began to read.



I got to the place in time, met others who came for the interview sitting down in the reception. I sat there too, everyone was busy pressing laptops, looking serious and all. Immediately I knew I had no chance, what exactly do I have to offer here, is like na only me no serious with my life. Will instill bring out that torn sheet of paper to read in this kind of setting 🤦

 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUPxpQ7JkGwUnrV5LeKAvYeWfeNWccnWEf9HTRfmXzgbT/1000996439.png 

Not long after, they began to call us in. The first lady went in, and in less than 5 minutes, she was out... Everyone started calling her..*\

* Well, she didn't answer anyone o, she was just smiling like someone that ate breakfast 💔 




Then the Jagaban was called, me, myself, and I.


I stood up with all confidence and went in.


*\

* I said, dragging the sittttttt when I realized I was sounding like... 😏


Omo, was I being sensible like that.



Then they asked me the first question...


*\

*

A very simple one at that, but my brain decided to go on a sabbatical leave at that moment. Everything just disappeared, I couldn't even make out what my name or surname was... 


*\

* That was what came out of my mouth.


Immediately I hold my mouth, smiled and began to say some confused things, from my name, to my hobbies and how much Nigeria is affecting me.

*\

* I concluded.



They looked at me with a kind of eyes, I was so sure they were thinking if I was okay, even i doubt if I'm really okay.


*\

* I responded almost immediately.


I didn't know if that was right or not, but then... I need a job.







Then another question was asked, and while answering it I went totally offline/offtrack.


https://img.leopedia.io/DQmT5cuCUbwmcrZJFYZkmr3G1khCHjNtyBrhdzzVHMFAqQg/1000996438.png


One of them told me that was not their question, guess what I responded with.



*\

* I said sounding so confident.


Truthfully, they are not related in any way.


Then came the last question...

*\

I responded quickly.

They just looked at themselves, smiled and asked me to step out for the next person.






🌹

**Images are AI generated.**



**Thanks a lot for taking your time to read through, kindly do well to stop by my blog @marsdave for more exclusive and amazing content.**

body.title: Pale Grass Blue
body.body:
| Latin Name | Observation Date | Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ***Pseudozizeeria maha*** | April 28, 2026 | Purulia, Natore, Bangladesh |


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQAUyz5Jyxe1XdeZ4gYBmUnupHRnCu7M6RXv9FhU81di2/20260501_194238.jpg)


On the afternoon of the 28th, I went to feed the fish in the pond. Suddenly, I saw something like a small insect flying. It was so small that at first I thought it was a fly or something like that. It was about the size of a fingernail, but when it sat on a green leaf, I looked closely and saw that it was a small butterfly.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUeFcDXyLNNLEe7XNBLgWqF5pc6DdJhgXw3fVKahev8zk/20260501_193341.jpg)

There was a lot of wind blowing because of the clouds in the sky, and those who do macro photography with mobile phones will understand very well how difficult it is to take a picture of such a small thing. As soon as I brought the phone too close to focus, it flew away and went to another place. I walked behind it for a long time and took some pictures, it was really a matter of patience. After taking the picture, I zoomed in and saw a black round spot surrounded by a white ring on its ash-brown wings. When it sat on a flower and drank the nectar of the flower, the scene looked quite beautiful.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW3u2VJ1EhikcEDosmikaD8HyPjUcvfPeiXW8ywNwwhSj/20260501_194833.jpg)

When I got home, I uploaded the picture to the iNaturalist app and found out that its English name is Pale Grass Blue. Its scientific name is Pseudozizeeria maha. They are so small in size that when spread out, their wingspan is 20-26 millimeters or 2-2.6 centimeters from one wing tip to the other. They are seen in abundance in grass, various flowers and crop fields in our Purulia or Natore area, but we usually do not notice them due to their small size.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuirJAxy7ftWg4VPpCTCQsiEb1LAcup121srB3ChvQSZ/20260501_194458.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWeTHBSmF9VRFvqeX2Ak2UKknbEPhdV3zkN76gMDmbmHU/20260428_141146.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTN5Aywd5XcXQsRotW4Du26cogQ9ed5i82b6B9ihNtXwG/20260429_134321.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXrfo2Mj4ZZMLjpWHGkUeLXLHJnVERwkDAkapGhgdqPqE/20260501_193636.jpg)

Let me know how you liked the pictures.

(All posts are written in Bengali and translated into English using Google Translate.)

body.title: The Final Battle Against the King. (Bramble The Mountain King)
body.body: Hellou mi gente de Hive Gaming. Hoy llega a su fin la aventura de Bramble The Mountain King.\n\n<span class=\
>Hello my Hive Gaming people. Today comes to an end the adventure of Bramble The Mountain King.\n\n

>Continuamos la partida en el pueblo donde habitan los no muertos y logramos escapar de ese lugar. Sin embargo, poco despues nos encontramos con el responsable de estos sucesos tan nefastos, se trata de una anciana llamada Pesta, el cual se la vio deambulando por el poblado. Este se nos aparece directamente por la espalda mientras intentamos cruzar un lago en un bote, nos manipula mentalmente y nos hace tener visiones donde nos ataca y tendremos que esquivar estos ataques.

>We continue the journey in the village inhabited by the undead and manage to escape from that place. However, shortly after, we encounter the one responsible for these dreadful events: an old woman named Pesta, who was seen wandering through the settlement. She suddenly appears right behind us while we attempt to cross a lake in a boat, manipulates our mind, and makes us experience visions where she attacks us, forcing us to dodge these assaults.

\n\n

>Superada la prueba, Pesta desaparece y logramos cruzar el lago para llegar finalmente a la isla donde se encuentra el castillo del rey de la montaña. Mientras subia a Ollie se le venian recuerdos a su mente de la aventura y de su impotencia de no poder haber protegido a su hermana. Dentro del castillo se encuentra nuevamente la biblioteca y hallamos la ultima parte de la Historia del Rey.

>Having overcome the trial, Pesta vanishes and we manage to cross the lake, finally reaching the island where the Mountain King’s castle stands. As Ollie climbs, memories of the adventure flood his mind, along with the anguish of not having been able to protect his sister. Inside the castle, we once again find the library and discover the final part of the King’s Story.

\n\n

>Según el libro, finalmente el rey encuentra a la bruja que con tanta ansia buscaba y el suplico una cura para su hijo. Ella lo ayudo dándole una flor que poseía gran poder y que se podía hacer tanto el bien como el mal. El plan funciono y el hijo del rey se recupero. Aun así, debido a las acciones nefastas que cometió el rey buscando a la bruja surgieron traidores que atentaron contra la vida del príncipe acabando así con la vida del joven. El rey detono toda su furia y utilizo la flor para hacer el mal y destruir el reino. La bruja contemplo este terrible panorama y decidió encerrar al rey en una gran montaña.

>According to the book, the king finally found the witch he had so desperately sought and begged her for a cure for his son. She helped him by giving him a flower of great power, one that could be used for both good and evil. The plan worked, and the king’s son recovered. Yet, because of the dreadful deeds the king committed in his search for the witch, traitors arose who plotted against the prince’s life, ultimately ending the young man’s days. The king unleashed all his fury and used the flower for evil, bringing ruin to the kingdom. The witch witnessed this terrible scene and decided to imprison the king within a great mountain.

\n\n

>Ya conocida la historia completa procedemos a abandonar la biblioteca y entramos a una habitación donde Ollie se viste con una ropa del pequeño príncipe. Resolvemos el acertijo del cuarto que impide que la puerta se abra para enfrentarnos finalmente al monarca de proporciones gigantescas.

>With the story now fully known, we leave the library and enter a room where Ollie dresses in the clothes of the young prince. We solve the riddle of the chamber that prevents the door from opening, to finally face the monarch of gigantic proportions.

>Después de subir a una meseta donde se encuentra una bolsa donde fue secuestrada la hermana de nuestro protagonista nos percatamos que estos trolls que secuestran a los niños son utilizados para alimentar al gigante rey que apenas se puede mover y en el acto vemos como Lillemor, es tragada por el gigantesco monstruo que pese a no quedarse a gusto enzarta con su tenedor al troll que lo alimenta para devorarlo también.

>After climbing up to a plateau where we find the sack in which the protagonist’s sister was kidnapped, we realize that these trolls who abduct children are being used to feed the giant king, who can barely move. Right before our eyes, we watch Lillemor being swallowed by the enormous monster who, still not satisfied, skewers the troll feeding him with his fork to devour him as well.

>En esta parte el rey se da cuenta de nuestra presencia y se desata una gran lucha donde debemos esquivar todo los que nos lanza y a la vez utilizar la piedra brillante para atacar a la zarza que tiene sobre sus hombros y que lo domina mentalmente. Derrotada la flor, el gigante cae desplomado y Ollie cae desde las alturas. Lillemor logra escarapar ilesa abriendo un lado del estomago. Ella logra cargar a su hermano Ollie herido mientras la montaña se cae a pedazos, sin embargo, Lemus el troll amigable sale sorpresivamente para ayudar a escapar a los jovenes. Así termina la historia.

>At this point, the king becomes aware of our presence and a fierce battle breaks out, where we must dodge everything he throws at us while using the glowing stone to strike the bramble on his shoulders that controls his mind. Once the flower is defeated, the giant collapses and Ollie falls from great heights. Lillemor manages to escape unharmed by opening a way out through the side of the stomach. She carries her injured brother Ollie as the mountain crumbles around them; however, Lemus, the friendly troll, suddenly appears to help the young siblings escape. Thus the story comes to an end.

/>

Realmente la experiencia con este juego fue positiva, la historia a pesar de no ser la mejor es suficiente para mantenerte a los mandos. La entrega gana tambien en el diseño de enemigos que realmente logra su objetivo, sumergirte en el terror, y la jugabilidad a pesar de ser simple logra su cometido. En mi opinion BTMK no es un juego que te enganche todas as tardes que tampoco es que destaque por la longitud de su historia pero si eres amante de este tipo de genero estilo Little Nightmare deberias darle una oportunidad, no te vas a arrepentir.

<span class=\

>My experience with this game was genuinely positive. The story, while not the best, is solid enough to keep you engaged. The game also shines in its enemy design, which truly achieves its goal of immersing you in terror, and the gameplay—despite being simple—gets the job done. In my opinion, BTMK isn’t the kind of game that will hook you every afternoon, nor does it stand out for the length of its story, but if you’re a fan of this genre in the style of Little Nightmares, you should definitely give it a chance. You won’t regret it.\n\n

/>

Hasta aqui el post de hoy, gracias por acompañarme de principio a fin en esta aventura. Nos vemos en la próxima. Hasta luego.

<span class=\
>That’s it for today’s post. Thank you for joining me from beginning to end on this adventure. See you next time. Goodbye.

body.title: A Family Trip to the Greenhouse
body.body:
Yesterday our family took a trip to a local greenhouse. This greenhouse is a treat to visit because it offers an abundance of tropical plants, right in the heart of Canada! 😄
-------------------

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXu29dfPhtZ7nYXiyQbw6wREXj291RFbouD2RkTFMxHmN/1777650537387.jpg)

Before arriving at the greenhouse, there was an opportunity to take some photos of the flora outside in the park as well. *Gage Park* is a lovely location, full of towering trees and colorful flowers. Here is my youngest and I admiring a *Grape Hyacinths.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSmLhzLxuDiFumqRu5svpjpP3ZcewHt4wkEVQ6s1FieCi/1777650537530.jpg)

Here, we have a wonderful *Juneberry* tree. I was surprised to learn that this tree will produce EDIBLE berries soon (most wild things are not edible), so I look forward to trying them

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQHswjgY7n43oFdsQ51GxoMt6wyyH2ZzrLEFAsUWjrAHq/1777650537699.jpg)

This is a *White Cherry Blossom* tree, one of my favorites. In my city, we are fortunate to have BOTH kinds of cherry blossoms: white and pink. These trees will produce juicy cherries to enjoy.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUuqmuLH5SxaFKuejkkXGtfemFV2rk4zGdrVpanQzNRrc/1777650537831.jpg)

Similar to the *Grape Hyacinth,* this flower is a *Dutch Hyacinth,* and they are some of my favorites. I simply adore the pinstripe petals, the way they burst forth. Funnily enough, the flower comes in an array of colors, but this was one of the only pink ones!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWg2HXu3upyodY6CCSSNKK8rYpC92puxguqqBatnbNhnq/1777650537954.jpg)

A gorgeous field of *Replete Daffodils.* I love the overlapping petals... They are truly a beauty to behold. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRcufM12wQE1WE12SZZBNMEwzar1haudJ1YFJh1pdyEv6/1777650579502.jpg)

We finally reached the greenhouse! 🙌 Immediately upon walking through the doors was a piano for children to play, so our girls went to town! 😄 They had a great time. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcCBhSUpgrUJmLBukcKoddmhzBHE4ovRC41gSmXyxy24Q/1777650579618.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZvrTnW3SuJ1iao3QHW4NWT3xxiP1WyrUurSMjdBwVB4g/1777650579718.jpg)

This is a beautiful *Tropical Hibiscus* flower 🌺 There were so many beautifully colored flowers inside the greenhouse, and the aroma was so sweetly overpowering. Every scent from every flower collided to create perfumed clouds...

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUPyEGfPC2krioZyCbKqStnasVhZPabbDCgsiojYYv2ft/1777650579840.jpg)

These cute flowers are *Clivia!* I thought they looked very sweet, all bunched together like this...

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcAy2T6XVvfmBcaZqZikj25kRRHR6Too9rujT7UKAPuJL/1777650579958.jpg)

This is *Mexican Honeysuckle.* As the name may imply, these plants are terrific for attracting pollinators, such as bees and hummingbirds.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW52wB3omkDK8uT37NkHVJ8QDuh9qhSKtUawFNpUP99tN/1777650611626.jpg)

Of course, there are some tropical trees in the greenhouse as well. This towering tree is called a *Giant White Bird of Paradise.* This tree must have been over 20ft. tall, and the leaves along were probably half of my height!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYJyLdMEzRbKk8trDKUA3o18iebc3wEQpwaEmW4F3HZFT/1777650611819.jpg)

This is a *Rainbow Croton* (not to be confused with crouton! 😂). Although it does not produce flowers, I find this plant to be incredibly beautiful all on its own. What a wonderful creation from God; every leaf produces its own unique color. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVgvtHd1xDoSoYYAatp3iwXf6ApTkm3za2UCawxsboz2H/1777650612007.jpg)

Some *Phalaenopsis Orchids* -- incredibly patterned petals. I love orchids, but these ones are so beautiful... Again, what a testament to God's creations, every petal possessing its own unique patterns...

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWs7YoatzqxRRswmQ3izRbGYZauEZAroAoTEwpreycF9b/1777650612117.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNnPxWR2CqgW6VYRFExePN9HUnkQn4rfMdY1rfDaw3nAG/1777650612282.jpg)

These are *Moth Orchids* (and I absolutely adore this name 🥰). Little baby orchids that pack a potent smell!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPPLTnUdGLr2vgPDUZd1QUj6iBVTXuj6UxnsqhE5HgrBs/1777650654760.jpg)

Another of my favorites; these are *Plumerias.* Similar to hibiscus, these Hawaiian flowers are very popular in making leis due to their vibrant colors and lovely scent. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVTSspJ2NYBvFwZgUKtshymvEPbvR36LB2xEteZoYPX38/1777650654861.jpg)

Here is another example of plumeria. I loved the pinks and yellows of this one, but unfortunately it was too out of reach. There wasn't really a way to capture a good photo, but I did my best 🙏

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWBwpSceY1zhF7wwnZJiSRexxhBbg1KvFHcQSZvWtitme/1777650654950.jpg)

This is a *Japanese Lantern.* This flower is so friggin' cute 🥹 The way its little \

dangles down! As you can see, there is no surprise as to where this plant's name came from. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd8KZjP5o5JZURX6ups5dXeconsGERz1oDnfzntWFzhty/1777650655100.jpg)

After leaving the greenhouse, we decided to walk around the park for a little bit. The birds and squirrels here are pretty domesticated (many people feed them), so we also spent some time with the silly little squirrels 😁 Here are some pictures of our girls playing hide-and-seek with a couple of them 😄

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYAJ1RXcUn7NrQtPQL3vtFfjmkPL2h9op5XD9L4xQDPaJ/1777650655260.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSY2N7JomkvgRqVFAZo2XeAuE1XFVG3AzAeN9F36neutW/1777650697013.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcpA8sLWbhyUqEB2JFEugS4yAHNNcmRD2Fg6rhLtVomi7/1777650697160.jpg)

We gave them a bit of food that we had on hand -- oats and peanut butter toast. They were so docile that they had no problem coming right up and taking the food from our hands! Obviously the girls had a wonderful time 😄

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbreS6Gf6LNnfc4TBgdZDCZ4fdmEe2Li6FRGvS6VpgrbM/1777650697285.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSpBikzmDqJ5smTbii94V9H47R1zhhoApojYktYc82Kvd/1777650697442.jpg)

Here is a fat grey squirrel who took his treasure up into the pine tree to feast 😂

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUctFoM89uvpfG44Jo8mqMyujECoxLbWE8NQfnUTDza8g/1777650697531.jpg)

A black squirrel, enjoying his piece of toast...

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXajUJpiYyjCzQbRpbbEKzkCevAMi2AiC85uZF5EMCo3b/1777650729661.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT767oFLXX9cZjTUjHubGsdGWLaKzTrRoWrGafsgp3ust/1777650729765.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPCgH2zrxaAPxWJqiEqfbQX29MCNZkg4z89eBXR64oB3P/1777650729933.jpg)

All in all, it was a wonderful day! 🙏 Being inside the warm, sweet-smelling greenhouse was very refreshing, and playing with the squirrels was a lot of fun, too 😊 Our girls had a great time! We will be sure to make more trips to the greenhouse soon...
--------------------

body.title: Mi vida últimamente | My life lately
body.body:
> Hola de nuevo! Hoy les traigo un nuevo post bastante chévere, esta vez de un nuevo set de fotos que he tomado a lo largo de estos días donde he estado haciendo varias cositas. He estado extremadamente ocupada estos días, y debido a nuevos cambios en mi trabajo todo ha sido muy cuesta arriba, sin embargo todo ha ido de maravilla y estoy muy contenta poruchas cosas que me han ocurrido. Hace unas semanas comencé clases y aunque como dije en una pública anterior que no comencé tan bien como creía, estoy con las mejores energías para realizar lo que tengo como meta, lo cual es, principalmente, pasar el semestre. Estas fotos las tomé a lo largo de estos días, y han sido días tumultuosos llenos de buenas y malas noticias, pero me enfoco más que todo en las cosas buenas ya que eso me motiva aún más, además de que lo malo siempre tiene solución. últimamente estoy optando por la mentalidad de ocuparme y no preocuparme, debido a que estresarme por osas que en verdad sí tienen solución no tiene mucho sentido, así que me estoy ocupando en mis cosas para que puedan salir de lamejor manera. Algo que siempre me hace feliz es caminar y apreciar lo que me rodea y lo hago en todas partes, en mi lugar donde vivo, en casa de mi novio y la universidad, siempre me gusta tomar fotos de las cosas lindas que veo. En este caso les traigo varias fotos que he tomado en estos días que me han gustado mucho, espero que les guste!
Hello again! Today I’m bringing you a pretty cool new post, this time featuring a new set of photos I’ve taken over the past few days while I’ve been working on various little projects. I’ve been extremely busy lately, and because of some new changes at work, everything has been really tough, but everything has gone wonderfully, and I’m really happy about the things that have happened to me. A few weeks ago, I started classes, and even though, as I mentioned in a previous post, I didn’t start off as well as I thought I would, I’m feeling super motivated to achieve my goal, which is, mainly, to pass the semester. I took these photos over the past few days, which have been tumultuous and full of both good and bad news, but I’m focusing mostly on the good things because that motivates me even more, plus, there’s always a solution to the bad stuff. Lately, I’ve been adopting the mindset of staying busy rather than worrying, because stressing out over things that actually do have a solution doesn’t make much sense, so I’m keeping myself busy with my own things so they can turn out the best way possible. Something that always makes me happy is walking and appreciating my surroundings, and I do this everywhere, where I live, at my boyfriend’s place, and at the university. I always like to take photos of the beautiful things I see. In this post, I’m sharing several photos I’ve taken recently that I really like. I hope you like it!

body.title: Composting my garden waste
body.body:
I have set up 2 composters in my garden, the green one I started already last year and the metal one was set up this year. Since I don't want to throw away the garden waste and the green waste leftovers from my fruits and vegetables I set up 2 composters to produce some nice compost of all the green materials that are growing in my garden and that I throw away, like cut grass leaves and weeds. 

One of the composters the green one I already started last year in summer so some of the material is already rotten quite a bit but it sill needs a little bit more time to turn into soil that I will be using to grow some vegetables in my garden. This way I can use the circular economy to save some CO2 by composting the leftovers myself instead of bringing it to a facility. The other benefit is that I will soon be harvesting some really nice compost / soil from this process.

![IMG_20260501_175830.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQTMiuB5HfzwiiG1aTbWaFHT1XfLRq29fFK2cFQfDuxwr/IMG_20260501_175830.jpg)
*Some green material, grass leaves and leftovers of fruits and vegetables. Picture: Florian Glechner.*


![IMG_20260501_175917.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQEtwVEBZ2n94QKXohmc6SEA4UqJ3g5FY5PrRNaqPdCKF/IMG_20260501_175917.jpg)
*Both of them are about 50% Plus filled at the moment*

# 2 Different Composters

Since one composter is a bit to less for most of my garden waste and the organic waste that I produce in my kitchen (which is only a very small fraction of the garden waste). I put up the second composter with only 4 stainless steel grids in my garden. I am already looking forward harvesting some of the nice compost soil next year or in the next 2 years depending on how fast the material dissolves into compost soil. For the bigger meaterial I have bought a shredder to shred the bigger parts into small parts so they dissolve and compost faster this way. With this 2 different kinds of composters I will also have some comparison between these 2 models. The open one which is only 4 grids and the more closed one that is made from plastic.

Usually it is good to have a great mixture of differnt green and brown materials on the composter so the decomposition will work faster, but  I have made a different approach and still try to mix some greens with browns. My intention is to have the green composter as my main composter for all the kitchen fruits and vegetables, since it is right outside the kitchen, and the metall composter is mainly used for all the grass and weeds and leaves and plants that are growing in my garden that I want to get rid of. This is some kind of convenience for me since I don't want to have such a long distance from the kitchen.

![IMG_20260501_180019.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPpi1zCKSpJ8xbzN8zyPn6oFqFDgnUg5Pz2cu1GScitsS/IMG_20260501_180019.jpg)
*Both of them are about 50% Plus filled at the moment*

# Environmental benefits

A lot of insects like invertibrates and worms live in my compost and help me to decompose the material I throw in there. There will not be any extra CO2 generated like when I put the waste into the \

which is a way a lot of poeple threat their green waste by giving it to a facility that is composting their material. But this material has to be transported to the facility that will produce some extra CO2 in this process. And of course I will not need to buy so much soil that will help me save money and also I don't need some extra CO2 by driving my car to bring the soil to my garden.  Another benefit for me is that this kind of producing compost soil is also much cheaper than buying it somewhere.

# Circular Economy 

Composting is a core pillar of the circular economy, transforming organic waste into nutrient-rich soil amendments, reducing landfill use, and cutting greenhouse gas emissions. By cycling nutrients back into the soil, composting improves soil health, sequesters carbon, and replaces synthetic fertilizers. It supports sustainability by closing nutrient loops

![IMG_20260501_175813.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQuHx138paJFLfduXe3768GCMFjA4ymShwcnBJEZrBkXY/IMG_20260501_175813.jpg)
*My main composter right next to the kitchen, for convinience. Picture: Florian Glechner.*

![IMG_20260501_175901.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNvG5FYGV25tjjfJ6XAhReFjrAt2xrXsw6GhKZb45VQyc/IMG_20260501_175901.jpg)
*My second composter is at the edge of my property hiding under a bush and tree so it is usually not visible in my garden. Picture: Florian Glechner.*

body.title: Ricebowl Blackpepper from Rotan Cafe
body.body:
>Hello, ASEAN.

Still on the topic of travel, and this time it’s about the food I discovered during a solo trip a while back. Of course, this isn’t anything fancy or specific to that region. It’s just a standard meal—the important thing for me at the time was that I wasn’t starving. LOL. That’s right, because it was already mealtime and I’d just stumbled upon this café. I’ve already written about this place regarding its coffee in a coffee community, but here, I want to share about the super cheap food that’s totally worth it. 

---


![FB_IMG_1776678820735.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23u62kAroiWmQfYHeDzBpWB6QbgsaANi13aMQNrP9fJ5eSGJJFQQARnCEEUyVzBKewH64.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678709623.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23u65ViU1zMyYDtnMEU8tvf6d5d5jgaCaw3oq2tdWNJKNaKTANBU8J4iwp3njh5TDRRAA.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678754544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/EpNnNT4pTn8JmAiq3KKTfp9fB75LdrLUjyQdFsCaa12K7guwSdm4BThFVUwPxBK5ZE5.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678784317.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/Eoc6xqHX2NfGH55BQ7E5WxAaWogi2fTojShqZVRBopEEe5FeVaF9aKcPtbyHZ53ytDW.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678786613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/243WRfk5Xgw4uswA6aruT1FEFqSFoESppVDBwd376mzrGGXZ841eEc7ESHtEPdNSEbNw3.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678812014.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xKraHxXKD2vq3SvFSesAhHq2ZGkJfYzdHe2TAWhswZ4P7CxvZ6fjMvqLbNR62QpEq72.jpg)

---

So this is one dish I picked randomly at the café. Since I don’t really like overthinking food choices, I just went ahead and ordered the black pepper rice bowl. And ta-da… a bowl of rice, chicken katsu, a fresh vegetable salad, and that super-aromatic black pepper sauce drizzled over the katsu. Just from the appearance and aroma alone, I was already sure this would be delicious, and sure enough, when I took my first bite, I felt so happy because the food met my expectations 

The white rice was cooked to perfection with just the right texture, paired with the warm flavor of the black pepper sauce. Not to mention the juicy chicken katsu and fresh vegetables. It’s a simple yet perfect combination. Effortlessly delicious! And what’s most surprising is the price. Just 20,000 rupiah (not even 1.5 USD) for this filling meal.  

---


![FB_IMG_1776678802551.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/EogMqcEJWDjcBdcr2dfXHdTpsHUE4kM2QJbjuTXMveWLQ77RbaW1pX1MdECpbS5TZgW.jpg)


![FB_IMG_1776678772011.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/Ep7v8SKZBWx91VhfqVmxA6pmHbPMNs9r4Zq5PoMasn8dh8Lq4ZYYVwHruDAvWfnvGit.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678795893.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/Ep5mmm88xn9jti5M9Qg3rpRNUR9UmarmdZ3319vX6UUhB9is1UaPXy1QGVGHDcEsq9e.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1776678788922.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/Eoc7XW9VAAWf4VigiA8gs54iTKULFxRVfs1bnohFLJ8LJz6Zenx4nHuonJQDCCfGSxK.jpg)

---

I savored it slowly because I also wanted to take a short break after walking a long way. And after this, my journey still has a long way to go. But that’s okay—I’m really enjoying this solo trip. Although the weather was a bit hot, I still felt it was within safe limits.

What do you think—is this meal really worth it? Share your experience if you’ve encountered similar things!

body.body:
![Messenger_creation_8A287BBA-2407-433D-BC60-750AF1C9D622.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSgwRTBJh9FiD7BBiaq5XHdnto1hQqQxR4n9iJLhznaJX/Messenger_creation_8A287BBA-2407-433D-BC60-750AF1C9D622.jpeg)

### Entertainment Industry 
The entertainment industry has its own wrongdoings and actual scams that many are not aware of. I remember a journalist who admitted to becoming a pimp, connecting aspiring actors and actresses to media bosses. There are also accusations of managers pimping the talent under their care to politicians. Even Megan Fox once likened the profession to prostitution. Furthermore, popular celebrities are often paid by those in power to leverage their influence. For instance, a well-known entertainment blogger was reportedly paid to criticize a singer's upcoming album, and a label executive allegedly sabotaged an artist who was once his wife. These scenarios are just the tip of the iceberg; much more may be happening without our knowledge.

### Friday 
It's been a fun day for us. We're able to support our sign language field service. I got to practice with driving. We also celebrated the graduation of our friend from SCE, as well as bonding with friends. Of course, my sister-in-law's cafe just opened. 

### A Month Ago

links.title: Jelly for Jam Makers: The Sweet Secret of the Ghost Factory
links.body:
/>
Deep in the German countryside lies a place where time seems to have stood still since 1990. Where once the raw material for millions of jars of jam was produced, ruins now stand guard over mountains of unused cardboard buckets and mysterious chemicals. This is the strange story of VEB Ogema – a factory caught between socialist industrial power, shattered dreams of the West, and a legend that comes alive at night in its empty halls.

/> On the outskirts of the town of Egeln, the ruins of a large industrial complex rise from a young forest. Egeln lies in the Börde, a region in eastern Germany known for its extremely fertile black earth soils and its long tradition of agriculture and food processing. From here, the communist-ruled part of Germany, the GDR, was supplied with raw materials for jam – today, it's haunted.

/>\n\nThe fine, odorless powder lies in open sacks on the floor, half-covered with leaves, but still brilliantly white, as if it had just come out of the extractor. On the windowsill stand bottles with the warning label \
still tightly sealed after more than 30 years, awaiting their use.\n\n

/>

Cardboard jam buckets

Matching cardboard jam buckets, like those used in East Germany for large containers of sweets, are stacked in piles, brand new. But the roof over what was once a storage room of the VEB Ogema consists only of individual slats and large holes. The abbreviation \
– the state-owned legal form for industrial companies in the planned economy of the communist era.\n\n

/>

Waiting in Vain

The last remnants of the production of the former staple supplier for East German kitchens wait in vain for collection. The sprawling buildings of the former chemical factory have been abandoned for decades. The steel pipe gate is rusted, the gatehouse with its iron weighbridge has collapsed.

/> Apart from amateur photographers and fans of the exotic charm of continued decay, hardly anyone ventures onto the 85,000 square meters on the northern edge of Egeln, which until 1990 employed almost 100 people. Through a complex chemical process, they extracted pectin from pressed apples and beets – the main products of the fertile Börde region.
/>\n\nFrom here, chemistry brought not only \
to the communist-ruled part of Germany, as the propaganda of the time proclaimed, but also the basic ingredient for tens of thousands of households. Ogema in Egeln – which translates roughly as \
– was responsible for the gelling agent that transformed fruit from their own harvest into a solid mass.\n\n

/>

Not a recession-proof business

A recession-proof business, at least until the end of German division in 1990. After reunification, the Pomos Pectin Works from the West German state of Hesse took over the factory site and the imposing brick buildings.

/> The change from a state-owned enterprise to a private investor from the West was typical for the period after the fall of the Berlin Wall. A beverage distribution business was added to the juice production, a legacy of which is still evident today in a mountain of colorful beverage crates. Ogema's rail connection, however, was shut down, and the tracks were dismantled.

/>

It was over

Then it was over. The Pomos Works went into liquidation. The Ogema property in Egeln-Nord became a lost place, one of those fascinating abandoned locations where one can witness how nature reclaims land that humankind seemed to have taken from it forever. The former state-owned enterprise was slated to become anything but. Then all sorts of things would happen to it. Plans dashed.

/> One investor wanted to build a horse slaughterhouse, another a solar power plant. A retirement home and a logistics center were also under discussion. The abandoned factory made headlines when a group of men ended up in court for illegally operating a car dismantling facility in the ruins. Now, silence has returned behind the rusty fence.

/> The chemical plant lives off its own legend: According to the tale, a former employee haunts the building as a ghost, searching for a chain he supposedly dropped into one of the pectin jars. He is said to roam primarily at night, and sometimes his clinking of jars can be heard as he searches.
